versions.changements: The requests of Nuée 1.0.0, before the protocol had a version: an engine that answers protocole with "Unknown request: protocole" speaks 1.0.

Nuée 1.1.0. New requests: protocole; retablir (Redo); the data steps, etapes, mettre_a_jour and retirer_etape; renommer_variable, supprimer_variable and type_variable; the versions of a project, fichier_change, fusionner and fusionner_finir; R-code models (the model type CODE) with empreinte_code, code_approuve and code_modeles; plugins (the model type PLUGIN) with greffons, greffon_lire, greffon_installer, greffon_retirer, greffon_projet and greffon_mettre_a_jour; resultats_cles and comparer_resultats; guide. New parameters: exemple's nom, ouvrir's lecture_seule and cache, enregistrer's auteur, reajuster's centrer, effets' echelle, ajouter_colonnes' colle, a model definition's meme_numero. New fields: Projet's retablissable, a_source and lecture_seule; ResumeModele's code_r and greffon; Modele's cles and an R-code or plugin model's own; annuler's documents, reajuster and a_reajuster, and retablir's; projets_modifies' ids; fusionner_finir's documents; RapportMiseAJour's changements_avant_etapes and its observations' distinguees; etat's code_interdit and greffons; error answers with fields of their own (arrete for a computation stopped, source_modifiee, code_non_approuve and empreinte, ligne, a plugin's refusal, a 409's fusion). Changed in a way a client of 1.0 notices: annuler keeps the model definitions added since the change (fitted models), which 1.0 took back with it; enregistrer without chemin no longer marks the project saved (it is a download); document_enregistrer and figure_enregistrer refuse an id the project doesn't have instead of making a new document or figure, and document_supprimer and figure_supprimer refuse it too; fermer_projet, rapports_vraisemblance, console and completer refuse an unknown project or model, which 1.0 ignored; exporter_prediction names its columns in the request's language; moyennes and puissance_tendance take only their own settings; an unknown model type or cross-validation is refused, not fitted as a PLS or validated by centres; an id is read as text (1 no longer names the first project); a missing projet or modele, an unknown observation and the choices the requests check get the engine's own messages instead of R's; most undo labels are in the request's language.

New request: paquet, the reproducibility package (a .zip of the project, its data as CSV with a data dictionary, one R script that redoes every model, its documents as reproducible Quarto files, a README, the licence of the data, CITATION.cff, codemeta.json and the SHA-256 of every file), with the DOI Zenodo reserved for the draft it goes in. New field: Projet's paquet, the answers kept from the last one.

New request: paquet_ouvrir, a reproducibility package opened again: unzipped in the engine's temporary folder, its files checked against its manifest, its project opened as a new project, with the results it deposited (ResultatsDeposes) to compare with its models fitted again. New parameter: paquet's qr, the QR code of its link. New fields: ouvrir's paquet_ouvrir (a reproducibility package, to open with paquet_ouvrir), Projet's depuis_paquet, the error answer's pas_un_paquet; paquet's .zip holds results/key_results.json (ResultatsDeposes), and with doi and qr, qr-code.svg.

description: The engine is the R script moteur/serveur.R of Nuée's sources (in an installed copy, the folder moteur of its resources). It finds Nuée's root from its own path, so it can be started from any working folder; it loads the engine (moteur/charger.R, every file of moteur/R) and the R console (moteur/console.R), then listens.
Both arguments are optional: the port, 8765 by default; the folder of the interface it serves at /, app/interface of the same tree by default.

It needs R 4.6 (the checks also run on R 4.1 to 4.3) with the packages jsonlite, httpuv, openxlsx, haven, readxl, RSQLite and ranger, and R's recommended packages foreign, nlme, mgcv, MASS, rpart and cluster.
Once it listens, it writes the line PRET <port> on its standard output: a client waits for it before its first request.
It listens on 127.0.0.1 only, and answers one request at a time (R has one thread): a long computation delays the requests that follow it.

Nothing stops it but its process: a client kills it when done. On Windows, bin\Rscript.exe only starts bin\x64\Rscript.exe, which is R itself: start the latter, or stop the whole process tree (taskkill /T).

Its temporary files (pasted tables, converted .usp projects, files exported without a path, the console's plots) go in R's temporary folder, under TMPDIR, TMP or TEMP: the application gives it a folder of its own for each run and deletes it when Nuée closes.

environnement.NUEE_JETON: The session's token (see jeton). The engine removes it from its environment once read, so that neither the console nor the programs it starts inherit it.
environnement.TMPDIR, TMP, TEMP: Where R puts its temporary folder.
environnement.CONVERTISSEUR_USP: The compiled .usp converter; without it, outils/export_project.exe, else convertisseur/export_project.py run by Python.
environnement.PYTHON: The Python that runs the .usp converter when it isn't compiled (python, or python3 outside Windows).
environnement.R_LIBS: An installed copy points it at the packages it brings along (Windows, macOS); the application also starts R with --no-init-file there, so that the researcher's .Rprofile stays out.
environnement.NUEE_CODE_SECRET: A secret the application draws at each start, which it alone sends with code_approuve, in the header X-Nuee-Code: only it approves R code (R-code and plugin models); without it, code_approuve adds the fingerprints it is given. The engine removes it from its environment once read.
environnement.NUEE_ARRET: The file whose appearance stops a long computation (the application's Stop): see Answers. Without it, nothing stops.
environnement.NUEE_SANS_CODE: 1 when the organisation's policy DisableCustomCode turns R-code models off, and lets only its own plugins run (etat's code_interdit).
environnement.NUEE_GREFFONS: The user's plugins folder, where greffon_installer writes; without it, no plugin is installed.
environnement.NUEE_GREFFONS_ORGANISATION: The organisation's plugins folder (the policy PluginsFolder), read only.
environnement.NUEE_VERSION: Nuée's version, which a plugin's manifest may require (nuee); without it, nothing is checked.

port.description: The first argument. The desktop application asks for 47863 when it is free (the interface keeps its settings per address), else any free port; a client chooses a free port of 127.0.0.1 itself and gives it.

description: The engine answers only the requests that carry the session's token: other web pages and other users of the computer reach 127.0.0.1 too, and the R console runs what it is sent.

The token is drawn by whoever starts the engine and given to it in NUEE_JETON: the application draws 32 random bytes, written as 64 hexadecimal characters. Started without NUEE_JETON, the engine draws its own and prints the address to open in a browser, http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/connexion?jeton=<token>.

Each request carries it in the cookie nuee_<port> (cookies don't tell ports apart: one name per engine), in its Cookie header: Cookie: nuee_<port>=<token>. Without it, or with another value, the answer is 403 {"erreur": "Request refused: it doesn't come from Nuée's window."}.
The Host header must be 127.0.0.1:<port> or localhost:<port>; any other name gets 403 with the plain text interdit, even with the cookie (a site whose name points to 127.0.0.1, DNS rebinding).

langue.description: The header X-Langue: en gives the engine's messages and texts in English; without it, or with any other value, they are in French. A few requests take the language of the text they write as a parameter instead (methodes, resultats_texte, script_r, document_reproductible; guide and comparer_resultats take one too, the request's language by default).

description: A request is POST /api/<name> with a JSON object of its parameters as body, in UTF-8; an empty body is a request without parameters. Neither the method nor the Content-Type is checked.

The engine reads the body with jsonlite::fromJSON(simplifyVector = TRUE): an array of numbers or strings becomes a vector, so a one-element array and its element are the same parameter; an array of objects becomes a table (a data.frame), which the requests that take a list of objects accept; an array of arrays becomes a matrix; an array mixing numbers and strings becomes strings; null is the same as leaving the parameter out.
Parameters the description doesn't list are ignored, though a request that changes the data keeps all its parameters but projet and apercu in its data step (etapes), saved with the project.

The engine reads most parameters with R's $, which also takes a parameter whose name starts with the one read when that one is left out (a few are read by their exact name). Send only the parameters a request takes.
The answer is written by jsonlite::toJSON(auto_unbox = TRUE, dataframe = "columns", na = "null", null = "null", digits = NA).

A vector of one element is written as that element: a field described as an array can arrive as a single value when it has one element, unless the engine keeps it an array (I() in its code). A table (data.frame) becomes an object of columns, each always an array; a matrix, an array of its rows; a missing value, NaN or an infinity, null; numbers keep all their digits.

Errors carry no code, only their message, said for a user in the request's language: a client tells them apart by their status and the fields some carry besides erreur, not by their words: conflit, date and fusion (409, enregistrer), arrete (a computation stopped), source_modifiee (retirer_etape), code_non_approuve and empreinte (an R-code model not approved here), ligne (an error in an R-code model's or a plugin's code), a plugin's refusal: greffon_non_approuve, empreinte, id and version; greffon_interdit; paquets_manquants and id; and pas_un_paquet (paquet_ouvrir: a .zip that isn't a reproducibility package). A malformed parameter often gets R's own message, untranslated. A few requests answer 200 with an error inside: series' tendances_erreur, raster_infos' erreur for a file it can't read, test_deux_variables' erreur for a pair it can't test.

Stop: the engine reads no request while it computes, so a client stops a long computation by writing the file NUEE_ARRET names (any content). The loops that look at it (permutations, cross-validation rounds, the AIC selection, boosting, simulations…: arret.R), five times a second at most, end the request at once: it answers 400 {"erreur": "Computation stopped.", "arrete": true}, the session put back as it was before the request (its projects, models, undo steps), the R console's log aside. The engine deletes the file when the next request comes, so that a Stop that came after the computation ended stops nothing.

statuts.302: /api/connexion with the right token: the cookie is set and the browser sent to the interface.
statuts.400: The request failed: {"erreur": message}, the message in the request's language (an R error, often one of the engine's own, said for the user).
statuts.403: Without the session's token: {"erreur": message}; code_approuve without the secret NUEE_CODE_SECRET in X-Nuee-Code, when the engine was started with one, likewise. With another host name: the plain text interdit. /api/connexion with a wrong token: the plain text jeton refusé.
statuts.404: A path outside /api/ that isn't a file of the interface: the plain text introuvable.
statuts.409: enregistrer only: the file changed elsewhere since it was read or written, {"erreur": message, "conflit": true, "date": its modification time, seconds since 1970, and "fusion": true when its changes can be merged instead (fusionner)}.

chemins./api/connexion?jeton=<token>[&...]: For a browser (development): with the right token, sets the cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/) and redirects (302) to /, keeping the address's other parameters (ouvrir=<path> opens a file). No cookie is needed.
chemins./api/fichier?chemin=<path>: The bytes of a file the engine wrote in its temporary folder (an export asked without chemin), as an attachment; any other path is refused (400, File not allowed). The cookie is needed.
chemins./api/televerser?nom=<file name>: The body is a file's bytes: kept in the engine's temporary folder under that name, then opened as ouvrir opens a file (its answer is ouvrir's). The cookie is needed.
chemins./api/deposer?nom=<file name>: The body is a file's bytes: kept in the engine's temporary folder under that name; answers {"chemin": its path}, for a request that takes a path (predire_fichier, the formulaire of kobo_apercu…). The cookie is needed.
chemins./: The files of the interface folder (the second argument), without the token: index.html, its scripts. Served with Cache-Control: no-cache.

client: Find R and its Rscript: on Windows, Nuée's own (resources\R\bin\x64\Rscript.exe in an installed copy) or R's (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\R\R-4.6.2\bin\x64\Rscript.exe for a user installation), elsewhere the one on the PATH.
Choose a free port of 127.0.0.1 and draw a token (32 random bytes in hexadecimal).

Start Rscript <Nuée>/moteur/serveur.R <port> with NUEE_JETON=<token> in its environment, and preferably TMPDIR, TMP and TEMP set to a new folder of the client's (and NUEE_ARRET, a file of that folder, to be able to stop a computation).
Read its standard output until the line PRET <port>; if the process stops first, what it wrote says why (a missing package, often).

Send each request as POST http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/<name>, with the headers Cookie: nuee_<port>=<token>, Content-Type: application/json and X-Langue: en (or fr), and the parameters as a JSON object.
Read the answer: 200, the result; 400 or 409, {"erreur": …} said for a user (arrete: true for a computation stopped); 403, a wrong token or host.
Ask protocole first: its version tells which requests and parameters exist (a 400 Unknown request: the engine speaks 1.0).
Projects (P1, P2…) and fitted models (M1, M2…) live in the engine's session, under the ids its answers give: they last as long as the engine, unless saved with enregistrer.
Stop the engine's process when done, and delete the temporary folder.

Colonne.description: A column of the project: a variable's number (its uid), or "id:k", the observations' k-th identifier ("id:1" their names; k as the rang of Projet's identifiants).

Groupement.description: What makes groups of observations, for a random effect, a cross-validation by groups or the time of an autocorrelation (regression.R: specs_groupement): an identifier of the observations by its name, or a variable by its number. Several arrive as an array of objects, a table for jsonlite.

by.description: "id" (an identifier) or "variable"; some requests also take "effets", the regression's random effects.

id.description: With by = "id": the identifier's name, as in Projet's identifiants (not "id:k").

pentes.description: A random effect's random slopes: the numbers of their variables.

chemin.description: The file written, or the first of them.

chemins.description: Every file written (always an array): a format without sheets writes one file per table.

Projet.description: A project's summary (serveur.R: resume_projet): what the interface shows of it, with the ids requests take.

id.description: The project's id in the session (P1, P2…): the parameter projet of other requests.

nom.description: Its name: its file's name, a sheet's name in brackets, or the name it was given.

source.description: The name of the file or table its data came from ("" when unknown).

modifie.description: Whether it has changes not saved yet.

chemin.description: The file it was opened from; null for a pasted table, an example, imported spectra or a summary by group.

table.description: The sheet or table of that file it was read from.

brut.description: A KoboToolbox or ODK export opened as it is, not imported.

annulable.description: The label of the change annuler would undo; null when there is nothing to undo.

retablissable.description: The label of the change retablir would redo; null when there is nothing to redo.

revision.description: Counts the changes of its data and their undos: a view that keeps a computation on the data computes it again when it changes.

chemin_enregistrement.description: Where saving writes without asking: the .nuee it was saved to, or opened from.

observations.description: The observations, as columns: uid, their numbers, and nom, their names (a project of one observation gives single values).

identifiants.description: The observations' other identifiers (site, year…), each {rang, nom}: rang is the k of "id:k"; without the .usp files' internal ones ($ClassID…) and empty ones.

variables.description: The variables with data, each {uid, nom, qualitative, categories (always an array), manquantes (missing values), temps (a qualitative variable whose categories are all dates or numbers, usable as a time), unite, description}.

jeux.description: The datasets of a .usp project, each {nom, n_obs, n_var}.

modeles.description: The model definitions kept in the project.

session.description: Whether the project holds a session of the interface (its views and fitted models), saved with it.

coordonnees.description: Its coordinates (spatial.R: coordonnees_projet): {x, y, the variables' numbers; systeme, an EPSG code or "plan"; nom_x, nom_y}; null when none are set or they no longer hold.

paquet.description: The answers of its last reproducibility package (paquet's meta), kept in the project and saved with it, as paquet cleans them: {titre, auteurs (each {prenom, nom, orcid}), description, mots_cles (always an array), licence}; null when it has none.

depuis_paquet.description: A project opened from a reproducibility package (paquet_ouvrir): {titre, doi (the package's own, null without), fichier (its .zip's name), manifeste (paquet_ouvrir's)}, kept for the session only, never saved; null otherwise.

kobo.description: The settings of the KoboToolbox or ODK import that made it, to make it again (kobo.R); null otherwise.

a_source.description: Whether its data came from a file it keeps as their source (a table opened, an export imported, an ODK archive's table opened as it is, the file of an update), which etapes describes and mettre_a_jour reads again.

lecture_seule.description: An old version opened read-only (ouvrir's lecture_seule): {source, oid, date}, as ouvrir was given them; null otherwise.

historique.description: The number of events in the audit trail a .usp file kept (the request historique lists them).

predictions.description: The prediction sets of a .usp project, each {nom, n_obs}.

Modele.description: A fitted model's results (serveur.R: resultat_modele for a PCA, PLS, OPLS, PLS-DA or OPLS-DA; resultat_regression for a regression; resultat_<type> of another analysis, analyses.R). The common fields first; each family adds its own, as noted.

id.description: The fitted model's id in the session (M1, M2…): the parameter modele of other requests.

nom.description: Its name (M3, or the name it was given; a refit is "M3 (1)"…).

type.description: PCA, PLS, OPLS, PLS-DA, OPLS-DA, a regression (LM, LMM, GLM, GAM), another analysis (RDA, CA, CCA, LDA, TREE, KMEANS, INDVAL, TRIM, PCOA, NMDS, PERMANOVA, MANTEL, FOREST, BOOST, DISTANCE), an R-code model (CODE) or a plugin's model (PLUGIN).

opls.description: Whether it is an OPLS or OPLS-DA.

A.description: PCA and PLS: its number of components (an OPLS: predictive and orthogonal); 0 for a regression or another analysis.

Ap.description: An OPLS's number of predictive components; 1 for a PCA or a PLS, 0 for a regression or another analysis.

K.description: Its number of X terms (a regression: the terms it kept; an analysis: its X columns).

noms_y.description: The names of its Y terms (always an array; empty for a PCA).

observations.description: A table, one row per observation of the model. PCA and PLS: t1…tA, u1…uA (PLS), T2, DModX, DModX_absolu, DModX_pondere, "<y> observé", "<y> ajusté", "<y> résidu" (PLS), classe, classe_predite, classe_predite_vc (PLS-DA), uid, nom. A regression: uid, nom, "<y> observé", "<y> ajusté", "<y> ajusté (effets fixes)" (a mixed model), "<y> prédit (VC)", residu, quantile_normal, levier and cook (LM), a column per random effect's level, groupe_vc. Another analysis: its own columns, with uid and nom. An R-code or plugin model: {uid, nom}, the observations given to its code.

reglages.description: Its settings in the form of the definition parameters, to modify it (nouveau.R: reglages_modele): type, x, y, classe, exclues, condition, echelles, blocs, modificateurs, transformations, A, G, vc, validation, aleatoires, correlation, famille, lisses, decalage, k_courbes, par_courbes, lisse_spatial, croises, croises_reglages, options, spectres, test, nom, titre.

numero.description: Its definition's number in the project (ajuster's numero), when the project keeps it.

app.description: Whether its definition was made by Nuée (and joins the project), not read from a .usp file.

test.description: With a test set (the definition's test): its predictions and statistics, {n, hors_domaine, observations, and for a PLS statistiques (y, n, RMSEP, biais, SEP, Q2ext) and classement (PLS-DA)} (jeu_test.R: evaluer_test; a regression's and an analysis's own). An RDA's or a CCA's test is its permutation test instead, {F, p, df, permutations}.

demande.description: The parameters it was fitted with, as the engine received them; {type, numero} for a model read from a file.

G.description: PCA, PLS, regressions and the analyses validated by groups: the number of cross-validation groups.

vc_par.description: What made the cross-validation groups (an identifier's or a variable's name); "" when the observations were dealt in turn.

composantes.description: PCA and PLS: a table, one row per component, composante, R2X, R2Xcum, R2Y and R2Ycum (PLS), Q2, Q2cum, valeur_propre; null for a regression.

variables.description: PCA and PLS: a table, one row per X term, terme, bloc, p1…pA, R2V_cum, Q2V_cum and p1_IC… (PCA), centre, poids, echelle, VIP, VIP_IC, w1, w*1… and their _IC (PLS); an RDA or a CA: its own.

variables_y.description: PLS: a table, one row per Y term, terme, bloc, c1…cA and their _IC, R2V_cum, Q2V_cum, centre, poids, RMSEE, RMSEcv.

coefficients.description: PLS: a table, one row per X term then Constante: terme, and for each Y "CoeffCS <y>" (centred and scaled), "Coeff <y>" (in the data's units) and each one's "… IC" (jack-knife half-width). An R-code or plugin model: a table, one row per coefficient its fit gives, partie, terme, estimation, erreur_type, statistique, ddl, p, bas, haut (the 95 % interval); null without coefficients.

limites.description: PCA and PLS: the limits T2Crit(95%), T2Crit(99%) and, with more terms than components, DCrit(5%).

RMSEE.description: PLS, regressions and some analyses: by Y name, the root mean square error of estimation.

RMSEcv.description: By Y name, the root mean square error of cross-validation.

seuil_vip.description: PLS: the VIP threshold found, {seuil, chute, marche, retenues}: the threshold, the drop at it, whether that drop is a clear step, the terms above it (statistiques.R: seuil_vip).

variance_t.description: PCA and PLS: each component's score variance.

ellipse.description: PCA and PLS: the squared radii of Hotelling's T² ellipse of a score plot, {95, 99}.

validation.description: PCA and PLS: how it was cross-validated, centres, sans_fuite or complet.

gardes_vc.description: PCA and PLS validated sans_fuite: the terms that kept the full model's weight in a cross-validation sub-model, with the group and the share of their standard deviation they kept (validation_croisee.R: gardes_vc); null when none did.

q2_vide.description: PLS and OPLS validated with recomputed centres: the Q2 of the empty model (each group predicted by the mean of the others).

gain.description: The model's gain over the empty model, (Q2cum − q2_vide) / (1 − q2_vide).

hierarchique.description: A PLS whose X are scores of other models: its honest Q2, each base model refitted without the hidden group (hierarchique.R: q2_hierarchique); null otherwise.

stocke.description: The components a .usp file stored with the model, as arrays R2X, R2Xcum, R2Y, R2Ycum, Q2, Q2cum.

version_origine.description: The version of the program that made a model read from a file.

groupe.description: A class model (modeles_classe): its group's name.

classe_modele.description: A class model: its class (the category it was fitted on).

cv_anova.description: PLS: by Y name, its CV-ANOVA table {source, SS, DF, MS, F, p, SD}.

classification.description: PLS-DA: its classification, fitted and cross-validated, {ajuste, vc}.

regression.description: true for a regression, false for another analysis; absent for a PCA or a PLS.

transformation_y.description: Regressions (and trees): the response's transformation, "" for none.

coefficients_regression.description: Regressions: a table, one row per coefficient, terme, estimation, erreur_type, ddl, t, p, bas, haut (the 95 % interval).

termes_retires.description: Regressions: the terms left out as redundant (a qualitative variable's reference category…).

termes_absents.description: Regressions: the combinations of categories never observed.

qualite.description: Regressions: the fit's quality, r2 and r2_ajuste (LM), marginal and conditionnel (mixed), or deviance_expliquee (GLM, GAM), then AIC, AICc, BIC, logLik, parametres, Q2, RMSEcv, echecs_vc, sans_categorie_vc, facteurs_vc; trees and some analyses: their own.

parametre_loi.description: Regressions with a distribution that has one: its estimated parameter (the negative binomial's θ, Tweedie's p, the zero-inflated Poisson's θ1 and θ2, the beta's φ).

courbes.description: A GAM: a table of its curves (edf, test).

decalage.description: GLM and GAM: the effort variable's name, with an offset.

dispersion.description: A Poisson model: its Pearson dispersion (χ² over the residual degrees of freedom).

gamm.description: Regressions: fitted by mgcv::gamm (a normal GLM or GAM with random effects and CAR1).

dans.description: With CAR1 in a finer level than the random effects: that level's name.

variances.description: Mixed models: a table of the random effects' variances, composante, terme, variance, correlation.

phi.description: With CAR1: its estimated correlation φ.

niveaux.description: Regressions: the random effects' levels, the widest first.

exclues_manquantes.description: Regressions and analyses: the observations left out for a missing value.

pentes.description: Regressions: the terms with a random slope, an array per random effect's level.

parts_variance.description: Mixed models: each level's share of the variance.

singularites.description: Mixed models with random slopes: the signs of a singular fit.

qualitatives.description: Regressions: the qualitative variables, those with adjusted means (moyennes).

signature.description: Regressions: what the AIC can compare (the response, its transformation, the observations, the kind of distribution and likelihood): two models of the same signature have comparable AICs.

prediction.description: Another analysis: whether it predicts new observations (predire).

chiffres.description: Another analysis: its line of figures for the explorer ("R2 0.70 · Q2 0.52 · 3 leaves").

vues_defaut.description: Another analysis: the views the interface opens first.

cles.description: Another analysis, an R-code or a plugin model: its key results as resultats_cles gives them, which a document cites ({{M1.<key>}}); absent when they can't be computed.

code_r.description: An R-code or plugin model: true.

n_donnees.description: An R-code or plugin model: the number of observations given to its code (N is its fit's nobs() when it has one).

code.description: An R-code model: its code, as it ran; a plugin's: the call, <function>(donnees, entrees, options).

classe.description: An R-code or plugin model: the R class of its fit (always an array, empty when its code returned no model).

reponse.description: An R-code or plugin model: its fit's response, when R gives it.

resume.description: An R-code or plugin model: what summary() of its fit prints, line by line (always an array).

sortie.description: An R-code or plugin model: what its code printed, 3,000 lines at most (always an array).

messages.description: An R-code or plugin model: its code's messages (always an array).

avertissements.description: An R-code or plugin model: its code's warnings (always an array).

autres.description: An R-code or plugin model: the other names of the list its code returned, besides modele, valeurs and tableaux (always an array).

images.description: An R-code or plugin model: its code's plots, 20 at most, each a data:image/png;base64 address (always an array).

statistiques.description: An R-code or plugin model: those of nobs, logLik, ddl, AIC and BIC its fit gives ([] when its code returned no model).

ajustees.description: An R-code or plugin model: {uid, nom, ajuste, residu}, its fitted values and residuals by observation; null when R gives none.

qq.description: An R-code or plugin model: {theorique, residu, pente, ordonnee}, the normal Q–Q plot of its residuals and its line; null without residuals.

valeurs.description: An R-code or plugin model: {nom, valeur}, the named numbers its code returned (list(modele, valeurs, tableaux)); null without.

tableaux.description: An R-code or plugin model: the tables its code returned, each {nom, n (its rows), colonnes, valeurs (one array per column, its first 1,000 rows)} (always an array).

paquets.description: An R-code or plugin model: the packages its code uses, as columns nom and version (null for one not installed).

R.description: An R-code or plugin model: the version of R it ran on.

comparaison.description: An R-code or plugin model: {AIC, signature} when its AIC can be compared with another fit's (the same signature), else {AIC, raison} or {raison}.

greffon.description: A plugin's model: its plugin, {id, version, empreinte, nom, description, licence, auteurs, citations, fonction, nuee, fichiers (their paths), manifeste ({entrees, options}, as Greffon), reglages ({entrees, options}: what was chosen), installe ({version, empreinte, source}, null without one)}.

ResumeModele.description: A model definition kept in a project (serveur.R: resume_modele).

numero.description: Its number in the project (3 for M3): the parameter numero of ajuster.

nom.description: Its name (M3, or the name it was given).

type.description: PCA, PLS, OPLS, PLS-DA, OPLS-DA, a regression (LM, LMM, GLM, GAM), another analysis (RDA, CA, CCA, LDA, TREE, KMEANS, INDVAL, TRIM, PCOA, NMDS, PERMANOVA, MANTEL, FOREST, BOOST, DISTANCE), an R-code model (CODE) or a plugin's model (PLUGIN).

A.description: Its number of components (0: chosen when fitted, or none).

ajuste.description: Whether it was fitted (in the file it came from, or by Nuée).

erreur.description: Why it couldn't be fitted, when it couldn't.

x.description: The names of its X terms (without a regression's factors that have no main effect).

y.description: The names of its Y terms.

stocke.description: The components a .usp file stored with it, as arrays: R2X, R2Xcum, R2Y, R2Ycum, Q2, Q2cum; null without them.

version_origine.description: The version of the program that made it, for a model from a file.

code_r.description: An R-code model or a plugin's: {empreinte, approuve}, the fingerprint of its code (the plugin's) and whether it is approved on this computer, so that it runs (code_approuve); null for another model.

greffon.description: A plugin's model: its plugin (greffons.R: resume_greffon_modele), {id, version, empreinte, valide, approuve, nom, auteurs (their names), interdit (the DisableCustomCode policy keeps it from running here), installe ({version, empreinte, source}: the installed plugin of that id; null without one)}; {valide: false, approuve: false, empreinte: null} when the definition has no copy of it; null for another model.

EtatFichier.description: What the engine knows of a project's file when it read or wrote it, to see before writing over it whether it changed since (serveur.R: etat_fichier). What the engine gives may carry two fields more, which ouvrir doesn't read back.

chemin.description: The file's path, made absolute, with / as separator.

date.description: Its modification time, in seconds since 1970.

copie.description: The engine's copy of the file as the project read or wrote it, in its temporary folder: the base of a merge (fusionner); absent without one.

sha256.description: That copy's SHA-256, kept once fichier_change compared contents; absent before.

EntreeJournal.description: An entry of the R console's log (console.R: noter); the engine keeps the last 1,500 to 2,000.

n.description: Its number: entries are numbered from 1 in the order they are written.

type.description: appel (an engine call the interface made, written in R), resultat (what R prints of a model just fitted), commande (a console command), sortie (its output), avertissement (a warning), erreur (an error, a console command's or a request's), image (a plot).

heure.description: The time it was written, hh:mm:ss.

texte.description: Its text, lines joined by \n; for an image, a data:image/png;base64 address.

ApercuKobo.description: The preview of the import of a KoboToolbox or ODK Central export with given settings (kobo.R: apercu_collecte), what the import dialog shows.

tables.description: The export's tables, the submissions table first, each {nom, lignes (its rows), parent (its parent table's name, null for the submissions table), principale (whether it is the submissions table), niveau (how many parent tables it has above it)}.

colonnes.description: The number of columns the import gives.

principale.description: Whether that table is the submissions table.

metadonnees.description: The metadata that can be kept, one per role present in the table or its parent tables, each {role, colonnes (always an array), garde (whether it is kept), nom (the role in words, in the request's language)}.

retirees.description: The metadata columns dropped (always an array).

parents.description: One per parent table of the imported table, nearest first, each {table, colonnes (the columns its import gives, which can be joined; always an array), choisies (those joined; always an array)}.

formulaire.description: The XLSForm form given: {fichier, titre, langues (its label languages, "" for the label column; always an array), langue (the one used)}; null without a form.

coordonnees.description: Whether the import gives the project coordinates (a GPS point, in WGS 84).

phrases.description: What the import does, one sentence per change, in the request's language (always an array).

Coordonnees.description: A project's coordinates as they are set and still hold (spatial.R: coordonnees_projet): two different quantitative variables and their system.

x.description: The number of the variable that holds x (the east, or the longitude).

y.description: The number of the variable that holds y (the north, or the latitude).

systeme.description: Their system: an EPSG code Nuée knows (4326, 2154…), or "plan" for plane coordinates in metres of an unstated system.

nom_x.description: The name of the x variable.

nom_y.description: The name of the y variable.

FichierLu.description: A file a project read, as it was read and where it stands now (etapes.R: etat_fiche): the source of its data, a step's table or raster, an import's XLSForm form.

chemin.description: Its absolute path when it was read, with / as separator.

relatif.description: Its path from the folder of the project's file ("donnees/releves.csv", "../releves.csv"), written when the project is saved; null before, or on another drive or server.

trouve.description: The file that would be read now: by relatif from the folder of the project's file first (a folder moved with its data), then by chemin; null when it is at neither.

existe.description: Whether it is found (trouve isn't null).

taille.description: Its size in bytes when it was read.

date.description: Its modification time when it was read, the computer's local time, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.

sha256.description: Its SHA-256 when it was read, in hexadecimal ("md5:" and its MD5 when an R older than 4.5 read it); "" when unknown.

lu.description: When it was read, local time, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss; "" when unknown.

modifie.description: Whether it changed since it was read: another size, or another modification time and a content whose fingerprint differs or can't be compared (a date alone changed, a copy, doesn't count); null when it isn't found.

actuel.description: Only when it is found: {taille, date}, its size and modification time now, written as taille and date.

RapportMiseAJour.description: What an update of a project's data changes, or would change (etapes.R: mise_a_jour, aligner_projet): the data the file and the steps give, compared to the project's by the names of the variables and the identifiers of the observations, what becomes of the models, the steps replayed and the file read.

observations.description: {ajoutees: the number of observations new in the file; retirees: the number of the project's that it no longer has; premieres_ajoutees, premieres_retirees: the names of the first ten of each (always arrays); cellules: the cells that changed in the observations and variables both have; cellules_par_variable: one per variable with changed cells, each {variable: its name, cellules} (always an array); par_position: whether the observations are matched by their place, no column naming them; repetees: how many observations of a same name nothing tells apart, matched by their rank among those of their name (on the side that has more of them); distinguees: the columns that tell apart the observations of a same name, by which they are matched (a year, a date, a survey number: identifiers and qualitative or whole-number variables both sides have, chosen one by one while one tells more apart; always an array, empty when names don't come back)}.

variables.description: {nouvelles: the names of the file's variables the project hasn't; absentes: the project's that the data no longer have, removed; recalculees: the computed variables missing from the file, computed again from their formula (each always an array); categories: one per qualitative variable with new categories, each {variable, nouvelles (always an array)}, placed just before its last; types: one per variable whose type changed in the file and was given back, each {variable, type: the type kept, qualitative (the file's numbers read as categories) or quantitative (its text read as numbers), perdues: the values that weren't numbers, now missing}; both always arrays}.

identifiants.description: {nouveaux: the observations' identifiers (secondary ID columns) new in the file; absents: the project's that the file doesn't have, without the .usp files' internal ones and the empty ones}, always arrays.

modeles.description: {variables_absentes: the models that use a variable or an identifier the data no longer have, which can't be fitted again, each {nom, numero, variables: those missing (always an array)}; observations_choisies: the models that left out rows they could fit and to which the file brings rows they could fit, to ask whether they take them (mettre_a_jour's sans_nouvelles), each {nom, numero, observations: the rows they fit now, admises: those they could fit outside their test set, nouvelles: the file's new rows they would fit}; sans_nouvelles: the names of the models that don't take the new observations, those of sans_nouvelles and those whose cross-validation groups came from a .usp file (always an array); nouvelles_categories: the models that take a term for a new category, each {nom, numero, variable, categories (always an array)}; references_changees: the regressions whose reference category changes anyway, their last one having no rows left, each {nom, numero, variable, avant, apres: the categories, null for none}}; every list an array, numero null for a model without a number.

etapes.description: One per step replayed, in order (always an array): {n: its number among those replayed; demande; etiquette, in the request's language; statut: ok, sautee (skipped: a variable, an observation or a category it names is missing, or nothing is left to do) or erreur; raison: why, "" for ok; notes: what a step done in part left out, the observations or categories it names that the data don't have (always an array)}. A skipped step doesn't stop the others.

fichier.description: The file read: {chemin: its absolute path, with /; table: its sheet or table, null for none; lecteur: how it was read, tableau, archive or collecte, as etapes' source says}.

notes.description: What to know of the file's reading (values read as missing…), always an array.

changements_avant_etapes.description: Whether the project is one from before 1.1 whose changes then aren't steps (etapes' conformes null): the update replaces its data with what the file and the steps give, those changes included, and the project is no longer such a project after it.

Conflit.description: A clash of a merge (fusion.R: conflit_fusion): something both sides changed differently since the base, or that one side removed and the other changed. fusionner_finir's choix settles it: what clashes is then taken from the side chosen (a model's definition or a figure whole, a document's clashing passages and fields, a variable's clashing cells, and its fields for a variable new on both sides; a thing removed on one side kept or removed).

id.description: Its id, the key of choix, the same when the same merge is prepared again: modele:<model>, document:<id>, figure:<id>, variable:<variable's key>, source; or champ:categories:<variable's key> (the order of its categories), champ:observations:leur and champ:observations:mien (observations removed on that side and changed on the other), champ:variable:<variable's key>:<field> (a variable's unite, description, formula…), champ:coordonnees, champ:prediction:<set>, champ:<field> (another field of the project).

genre.description: modele, document, figure, variable (a variable's or an identifier's values, or a variable removed on one side and changed on the other), source (both sides updated the data from different files) or champ (anything else, as its id says).

cle.description: What it names: the model's name, the document's or figure's id, a variable's key (its name, followed by U+001F and its rank when several variables have it; for an identifier of the observations, U+001D, id: and its name), <variable's key>.<field>, observations, coordonnees, source, the prediction set's name or the project field's.

titre.description: Its title, in the request's language: "Model M3", "Document “Report”", "Figure “Map”", "Variable “x1”", "Identifier “site”", "Order of the categories of “zone”", "Unit of “x1”", "Observations removed on their side, changed on mine", "Coordinates", "Data source", "Prediction set “2024”", "Project field “format”"…

mien.description: What my side did, in a few words, in the request's language: "M3: 2 component(s) → 4 component(s); X: + x5", "paragraph 3 rewritten", "unit: kg; 2 cell(s): S1: 4 → 5, S2: 3 → empty", "data updated from releves.csv", "changed", "removed"…

details.description: What else to show, by genre; null when there is nothing more (a document or figure removed on one side and changed on the other, a variable's field, the coordinates, a prediction set, a project field). modele: {champs}, the definition's fields changed both ways (x, y, A, condition…), or ["retire"] when one side removed the model. document: {passages, each {ligne (the number in my text of its first paragraph, each line that isn't empty being one, as the editor shows them; where it would be, when I removed it), base, mien, leur (its lines in each version, joined by \n)}; champs, its titre, langue, bib or style changed both ways}. figure: {champs}, titre or contenu. variable: {n, the number of cells changed both ways; cellules, the first 100, each {observation (its name; "S1 (2)" for the second of that name), base ("" when the base didn't have that observation), mien, leur: values as text, numbers to 6 significant digits with the request's decimal mark, "empty" for a missing value}}, with champs (the fields that differ) for a variable new on both sides and made differently, or {champs} alone when only its fields differ; {retiree: "mien" | "leur"}, the side that removed the variable the other changed. source: {mien, leur}, the names of the files each side updated the data from. champ, the order of a variable's categories: {base, mien, leur}, the categories common to the three in each one's order; observations removed and changed: {observations}, their names. Every array in details stays an array.

Greffon.description: A plugin as the engine shows it (greffons.R: greffon_interface): who it is, where it comes from, whether it is well formed and may run here, its packages, and, from a manifest without errors, its card and the inputs and options its models' dialog asks (vues_greffons.js); those fields from the manifest are absent when it has errors.

id.description: Its id, as its manifest writes it, even a manifest with errors (a folder that can't be read: the folder's name); null when the manifest has no id in text.

version.description: Its version as its manifest writes it (X.Y.Z when valid); null when it has none in text.

source.description: utilisateur (the user's plugins folder), organisation (the organisation's), fichier (a file greffon_lire read), projet (the copy a project's model keeps).

dossier.description: Its folder, for the user's and the organisation's; null otherwise.

etat.description: ok; invalide (it has errors: erreurs; it doesn't run); double (a folder of the same source listed before it has its id: this one isn't used); remplace (the user's, of an id the organisation also gives: the organisation's is used). A file's or a project's copy: ok or invalide.

empreinte.description: Its fingerprint, the SHA-256 of its files in a fixed order (64 hexadecimal characters; greffons.R: empreinte_greffon), what code_approuve approves; null for a folder that couldn't be read.

permis.description: Whether it may run on this computer: the organisation's (its fingerprint), or approved here (code_approuve) while the DisableCustomCode policy is off.

trop_recent.description: Whether its manifest asks for a newer Nuée than this one (nuee).

erreurs.description: What is wrong with it, each saying where and why ("inputs[2].accepts: …"), in the request's language (always an array, empty when it is well formed).

avertissements.description: What is worth saying without being wrong (texts without French) (always an array).

paquets.description: The R packages its manifest asks for, as columns, each always an array: nom; present, whether the R Nuée uses has it; version, its version (null when absent).

nom.description: Its name, {en, fr} (fr: the English when the manifest has no French).

nuee.description: The version of Nuée it needs at least, X.Y.Z.

fonction.description: The name of its R function, called <fonction>(donnees, entrees, options).

auteurs.description: Its authors, each {nom, orcid (without https://orcid.org/; null without)}.

citations.description: How to cite its method, each {texte, bibtex (null without)} (always an array, empty without).

entrees.description: The project's variables its dialog asks for, each {id, type (variable: one; variables: several), accepte (quantitative, qualitative or any), min, max (null: no maximum), facultatif, libelle ({en, fr}), aide ({en, fr}; null without)} (always an array).

options.description: Its settings, each {id, type (number, choice, checkbox or text), libelle, aide, defaut, and for a number min, max (null without) and entier, for a choice valeurs ([{valeur, libelle}])} (always an array).

fichiers.description: greffon_lire and greffon_projet only: its files, each {chemin, texte}, plugin.json then the R files its manifest lists.

ResultatCle.description: A key result of a fitted model (resultats_cles.R: entree_resultat): a number, or a category, under the key a document cites and What changed compares; a field it doesn't have is absent.

cle.description: Its key, the same from one fit to another and in both languages: the reference a document cites ({{M1.Q2}}: Q2; {{M1.coef.annee}}: coef.annee); unique in a summary.

libelle.description: What it is, in the request's language, without an article ("Cumulative Q²", "Coefficient of “annee”").

groupe.description: ajustement (the fit's statistics), estimations, tests, aleatoires (random effects), composantes (per component), variables (per variable: VIP, coefficients, loadings), especes (indicator species), moyennes (adjusted means), puissance (trend power), jeu_test (the test set), stocke (results a .usp file stored).

valeur.description: The number; absent for an entry that is a category only.

n.description: Its count (the observations, presences or test set observations it rests on).

limite.description: An estimate's null value, 0 (1 for a multiplicative slope, an index, a ratio): crossing it is changing sign, and without p an interval that excludes it makes it significant.

repere.description: A threshold of the value itself (1 for a VIP).

forme.description: pourcentage (a share, written in %) or entier.

genre.description: f when its label is feminine in French, for the French sentences.

alias.description: The other references a document can cite for it (est.annee, ic.annee and p.annee for coef.annee; <key>.ic, .bas, .haut, .p, .pourcent… for another analysis's entry) (always an array).

axe.description: The component of a value whose sign is arbitrary (a PCA loading: "1", "2"…), which comparer_resultats turns the other fit's way.

classe.description: A category that goes with the value or makes the entry: TRIM's trend class, an indicator species' group, the detection function chosen, the most important variable, the first split's.

classe_texte.description: That category in words, when its code doesn't read (TRIM's class).

ResultatsDeposes.description: A reproducibility package's key results, its file results/key_results.json (resultats/resultats_cles.json in a French package; paquet.R: json_resultats_paquet): written by paquet from the latest fit of each model in the session, read back by paquet_ouvrir, its numbers to 15 significant digits.

nuee.description: The version of Nuée that wrote it (paquet's version).

paquets.description: Every R package loaded then but R's own (base, stats, utils…), its version under its name.

langue.description: The package's language, that of the labels: fr or en.

doi.description: The package's own DOI (paquet's doi), null without.

modeles.description: Each model, in the order paquet got them: {nom, numero, titre, type (ResumeModele's: PCA, OPLS-DA, LM…), A (its fit's number of components, which a fit again takes; 0 for a regression or another analysis), entrees (ResultatCle[], as resultats_cles gives them, in the package's language)}, or, for a model the package doesn't redo (its categories changed since its fit, not fitted: paquet's non_ajustes), {nom, numero, titre, type, erreur} (always an array).

type.description: The model's type; another value is refused (Unknown model type). verifier also takes CLASSES (the class models' PCA, without the class).

valeurs.PLS-DA: PLS discriminant analysis, its Y the categories of classe
valeurs.OPLS: orthogonal PLS, as many predictive components as Y
valeurs.OPLS-DA: orthogonal PLS-DA, as many predictive components as classes less one
valeurs.CODE: a model written in R by the user (code.R): its options' code, run when approved on this computer
valeurs.PLUGIN: a model of a plugin (greffons.R): its options' greffon, entrees and options

x.description: The X variables' numbers (a qualitative variable enters by its categories). A PCA, PLS or OPLS needs at least one; a regression without X is the intercept-only model; another analysis reads the roles it needs. With spectres, they are taken in the table's order.

y.description: The Y variables' numbers: PLS and OPLS (one or more), a regression (exactly one, quantitative), an analysis with responses (RDA, CCA…). A PLS-DA takes classe instead.

classe.description: PLS-DA and OPLS-DA: the qualitative variable whose categories are the classes (only the observations of a known class enter); LDA and a classification tree: their class variable.

exclues.description: The observations left out of the model (unticked), by their numbers (Projet's observations.uid).

echelle.description: The scaling of the terms that have none in echelles.

valeurs.UV: centred and divided by the standard deviation
valeurs.Par: Pareto: centred and divided by the square root of the standard deviation

A.description: PCA, PLS and OPLS: the number of components; 0 chooses it by the automatic fit (nouveau.R: autoajuster, cross-validation and the published rules). An OPLS has at least its predictive ones. Ignored by regressions and the other analyses.

nom.description: The model's name; by default M<n + 1>, n the number of definitions in the project. A definition of the project with that name is replaced by this one (Model › Modify model).

G.description: Without vc: the number of cross-validation groups, the observations dealt to them in turn.

transformations.description: By variable, its transformation: {"<variable number>": "racine2" | "racine4" | "log10" | "log10:C2" for log10(x + C2) | "ln:C1:C2", "neglog:C1:C2" (−log10), "exp:C1:C2", "lineaire:C1:C2" or "log10:C1:C2" of C1·x + C2 | "logit:C1:C2" between the bounds C1 < C2 | "puissance:C1:C2:C3" for (C1·x + C2)^C3, "puissance:C3"}. A qualitative variable isn't transformed.

croises.description: Cross terms and powers, each the numbers of two or more X variables: [[3, 5], [4, 4]] for v3·v5 and v4². A qualitative variable enters once at most, by each of its categories. In a regression, a factor that isn't in x enters without a main effect (y ~ a + a:b).

croises_reglages.description: By cross term, named by its variables' numbers in order ("3*5"): {echelle, bloc, modificateur}; without it, the default scaling, neither block nor modifier.

spectres.description: Spectral preprocessing, applied in order to each observation's quantitative X: {type: "snv"}, {type: "msc"}, {type: "sg", derivee (0), fenetre (11: odd, 3 or more), degre (2)}, {type: "detrend", degre (2)}, {type: "ligne_base"} (spectres.R). Not for a regression.

test.description: The observations of a test set: left out of the model, then predicted by it (Modele's test). The analyses that don't predict refuse one.

vc.description: What makes the cross-validation groups: an identifier ({by: "id", id: its name}) or a variable ({by: "variable", variable: its number}), one group per value; absent, or {by: "order"}: G groups in turn. A mixed model without it is validated by its first random effect.

blocs.description: By variable, the name of its block: block weighting, each term's weight divided by the square root of its block's number of terms; in a regression, only the groups of the contributions table (apports).

modificateurs.description: By variable, a factor multiplying its weight (1: none).

aleatoires.description: Regressions: the random effects, nested from the widest to the finest, three at most, each an identifier or a qualitative variable; its pentes: the quantitative X variables (terms on their own) with a random slope at that level. An LMM needs one, an LM takes none.

correlation.description: Regressions with random effects: {type: "CAR1", temps: a Groupement, the time (an identifier or a quantitative variable), dans: a Groupement, a finer level than the last random effect (optional)}: a CAR1 autocorrelation within those groups, a single time per group. A GLM or GAM takes it only with the normal distribution (mgcv::gamm).

famille.description: GLM and GAM: the response's distribution.

lisses.description: GAM: the quantitative X variables fitted as smooth curves, s(x).

decalage.description: GLM and GAM with a log link (poisson, binomiale_negative, gamma, tweedie, poisson_zi): the effort variable, offset(log(effort)).

k_courbes.description: GAM: by curve's variable, its basis dimension k, a whole number from 3 to 100 (10 at most without it).

par_courbes.description: GAM: by curve's variable, the number of a qualitative X variable that is also a term of the model: a curve per category, s(x, by = f).

lisse_spatial.description: GAM: a spatial smooth of two quantitative coordinates, {variables: [x, y], base: "tp" (thin plate, the default) or "sos" (on the sphere, longitudes and latitudes in degrees), k: a whole number from 5 to 300}.

options.description: Another analysis's own settings, which its ajuster_<type> reads (analyses.R). An R-code model (CODE): {code}, its R code, a text or an array of lines, whose last value is the fitted model (or list(modele, valeurs, tableaux)); it sees the model's observations as donnees, one column per variable. A plugin's model (PLUGIN): {greffon: {id, empreinte (a version by its fingerprint; by default the installed one)}, entrees: {<input id>: variable numbers}, options: {<option id>: value}}, checked against its manifest (Greffon's entrees and options). Both ignore x, y, the scalings, A and the cross-validation, and take no test set.

condition.description: Keep only the observations where this R expression is true (condition.R: the project's variables and identifiers, numbers, text and a fixed list of functions), evaluated again at each fit; a missing value counts as false.

validation.description: PCA, PLS and OPLS: how cross-validation is done; another value is refused (Unknown cross-validation).

valeurs.centres: only the centres recomputed without the hidden group
valeurs.sans_fuite: centres and weights recomputed; a term nearly constant without the group keeps the full model's weight

erreur_code.quand: An R-code model's code stopped with an error or doesn't parse, or a plugin's code failed (code.R: erreur_code; greffons.R: erreur_greffon). erreurs.message: Nothing to undo
erreurs.quand: The project has no undo step left (also for an id that is no project's).

erreurs.message: <R's own message>
erreurs.quand: projet is left out: the undo stack is read before the project, so the answer is R's attempt to select less than one element in get1index, untranslated, not projet_manquant.

annuler.effet_detail: The project goes back to its state before its last change that has an undo step (20 are kept per project), its data source and data steps included; that step goes to the redo stack (retablir, Edit › Redo; 20 kept too), which the next change with an undo step empties. Its documents, figures and the state of its file stay as they are now, and it counts as modified, but for two changes: undoing a merge (fusionner_finir) gives back the documents, figures and file state it had before the merge when they haven't changed since, and undoing a renamed variable puts back the document references that followed it, even in a document written since. The session's models whose observations came from a condition of the project follow its condition back. A model defined since the change (fitted, which has no undo step of its own) stays in the project, its observations and categories brought to the data back, unless it reads a variable or a category the undo takes away (a computed variable, the BACI variables, merged categories): it goes with them, and Redo brings it back; it keeps its number unless a model back has it. A model the change itself added (baci_modele's mixed model, the other side's in a merge, the console's) goes with the change. A variable number the undo frees isn't given again to another variable.

retablir.but: Redoes the last change of a project that Edit › Undo took back, as Edit › Redo (Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z) does.

projet.description: The project as the change redone left it: its annulable that change again, its retablissable the next one to redo.

etiquette.description: The label of the change redone ("data update", "sugar renamed brix"…), as Projet's retablissable gave it, written when the change was made.

documents.description: The ids of the documents whose text the redo changed (a renamed variable's references, a merge's documents), for a client to read them again (always an array).

reajuster.description: Whether the change redone replaced the project's data (a data update, a removed step: mettre_a_jour, retirer_etape): every model of the session made from the project is then to be fitted again on the data as they now are, as the interface does in each of its windows.

a_reajuster.description: The numbers of the project's models whose fit in the session is on variables that are no longer the project's once the change is redone (a name given back, a variable removed or retyped, a category renamed): reajuster now refuses to fit them as the session has them, so a client fits them again from the project (ajuster with numero). Always an array, sorted.

erreurs.message: Nothing to redo
erreurs.quand: The project has no change to redo: none was undone since its last change that has an undo step (which empties the redo stack); also for an id that is no project's, or a project closed since.

erreurs.message: <R's own message>
erreurs.quand: projet is left out: the redo stack is read before the project, so the answer is R's attempt to select less than one element in get1index, untranslated, not projet_manquant.

retablir.effet_detail: The project takes back the state the last undo took it from: its data, source, steps and model definitions as the undo step kept them (so a definition added or changed since the undo, fitted or with a note written, leaves nothing to redo: such a change empties the redo stack, as a change with an undo step does; fitting one of the project's models again by its number, ajuster with numero, doesn't). Its documents, figures, the state of its file and where it saves stay as they are now, but a merge's come back while unchanged since the undo, and a renamed variable's references in the documents follow the new name again; it counts as modified, and the session's models whose condition came from their definition follow it. The entry moves from the redo stack to the undo stack, so Edit › Undo takes it back again, in one step; the redo stack keeps 20 entries per project, empties at any new change that has an undo step (memoriser) and goes when the project closes.

enregistrer.but: Saves a project as a .nuee file, with the interface's session.

chemin.description: The file to write (a .nuee). Without it, <project's name>.nuee in the engine's temporary folder, for a browser to fetch with /api/fichier: a download, which doesn't count as saving the project.

session.description: The interface's session (its views and fitted models), JSON text only it reads: kept with the project and saved with it.

ecraser.description: true to write even when chemin is the project's file and that file changed elsewhere since the project read or wrote it.

version.description: Nuée's version, written in the file (its nuee field) with R's and the packages'.

auteur.description: Who saves, as the settings of the versions name them: a name, or {nom, email}, of which only nom is kept. Written in the file (its nuee field's auteur, without the spaces around it), so that a colleague who opened the same file sees who changed it (fichier_change, fusionner); without it, or empty, the file names nobody.

chemin.description: The file written.

erreurs.message: This old version is read-only: Save as keeps a copy elsewhere.
erreurs.quand: The project is an old version opened read-only (ouvrir's lecture_seule) and chemin is the temporary file it was read from.

erreurs.message: Folder not found: <folder>
erreurs.quand: chemin's folder doesn't exist.

erreurs.message: <file> was changed elsewhere since you opened or saved it.
erreurs.quand: chemin is the file the project was read from or last saved to, it changed since (its size or modification time), and ecraser isn't true. The answer is HTTP 409: {"erreur", "conflit": true, "date": the file's modification time in seconds since 1970, and "fusion": true when the engine kept a copy of the file as the project read or wrote it, so that its changes can be merged (fusionner) rather than written over}.

erreurs.message: Couldn't write <chemin>
erreurs.quand: The file, written first in the engine's temporary folder, can't be copied into chemin's folder (a folder that can't be written).

enregistrer.effet_detail: With chemin, the file is written first in the engine's temporary folder, then copied into place, replacing an old one only once the new one is whole; that copy stays, the base of a later merge (fusionner). The project then counts as saved, later saves go there, the file's state is kept to see a change made elsewhere, the paths of its data source and step files are written relative to the file's folder, and an old version opened read-only becomes a project like any other. Without chemin, only the file to download is written, and the project stays modified or not as it was. The session given is kept with the project.

ouvrir.effet_detail: Opens a new project (with secours or origine, marked modified; with cache, hidden from etat). A .nuee or .json file is first copied into the engine's temporary folder and read from that copy, which is kept as the base of a later merge (fusionner) unless the project is a recovery copy, a read-only old version or hidden. A table, an export imported with kobo, or an ODK archive opened as it is keeps where its data came from (its data source: the file, its table, what the import decided of its columns, its size, date and SHA-256; Projet's a_source) and starts its data steps, which Update the data replays on that file read again. A file with several tables, or a KoboToolbox or ODK export to preview, opens nothing; the export's reading is kept in a cache.

erreurs.quand: No column is left to add.

erreurs.message: The key “<key>”<columns> comes <n> times in the table<, as do <k> other(s)>: each key must come at most once (add to the key the column that tells these rows apart, the year for instance)
erreurs.quand: A key is on several rows of the table.

erreurs.message: No observation finds its key<columns> in the table: nothing was added. Keys are compared as written (S1 isn't s1, nor 01 1); the project has <keys>, the table <keys>.
erreurs.quand: No observation's key is in the table.

erreurs.message: <the reader's message>
erreurs.quand: The file is missing or can't be read: the message of R or of the package that reads it, often untranslated.

ajouter_colonnes.effet_detail: One undo step (columns from <nom>), also noted as a data step, which Update the data replays: it keeps the table's file as the project keeps its source (its path, size, date and SHA-256), or the pasted cells' text. Numbers make quantitative variables, the rest qualitative ones; the models already fitted don't change.

raster_infos.but: Says what each raster file is and how many observations fall inside it, or why it can't be read, before ajouter_raster adds its values.

projet.description: The project's id; its coordinates must be set.

chemins.description: The raster files' paths: GeoTIFF (.tif) or ESRI ASCII grids (.asc).

fichiers.description: One per path, in their order (always an array). A file read: {chemin, nom, taille (bytes), format (GeoTIFF, BigTIFF or ASCII), largeur, hauteur (cells), bandes, type (uint8, int16, float32…, texte_entiers or texte for an ASCII grid), compression ("" without), predicteur, organisation (tiles or strips, in words), bandes_separees, resolution (the cells' size, in words), etendue {xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax} in its system, systeme {code (null when unknown), nom, suppose: taken as the project's for want of its own}, nodata (null without), palette, pixel_point, methode (the method proposed: cellule for classes, bilineaire otherwise), noms (each band's proposed name), noms_libres (the names they would take in the project), dedans (the observations inside), observations (those with coordinates), total, notes (always arrays for noms, noms_libres and notes)}. A file that can't be read: {chemin, nom, taille (null when missing), erreur: why, in the request's language}.

raster_infos.effet_detail: A file that can't be read doesn't fail the request: its entry says why in erreur.

ajouter_raster.but: Adds the values of raster files at the observations' coordinates as new variables, one per band (Edit › Add raster values).

projet.description: The project's id; its coordinates must be set.

fichiers.description: The files, each {chemin: its path; methode: how a value is read, cellule (the cell holding the observation), bilineaire (interpolated from the four nearest cells), moyenne or majorite (the mean, or the majority class, of the cells within rayon), another or none being the method raster_infos proposes; rayon: the circle's radius in metres, for moyenne and majorite, at most 50000; noms: one name per band, by default the names raster_infos proposes}. Bands of different files given the same name make one variable, as tiles of one raster: they must then share their method and radius.

resultat.description: The project with the new variables.

raster.description: {variables: one per variable added (always an array), each {nom: its name ("name (2)" for a name taken), demande: the name asked, fichiers (always an array), methode, rayon (null without), valeurs: the observations with a value, sans_coordonnees, hors: outside the raster, sans_valeur: on a cell without a value, note: the files' notes, null, one string or several}; phrases: what happened, in sentences, one alone coming as a string}.

erreurs.message: Choose at least one raster file.

erreurs.quand: Every observation lacks a coordinate.

erreurs.message: File not found: <path>

erreurs.message: <file>: Nuée reads GeoTIFF rasters (.tif) and ESRI ASCII grids (.asc). For another format, export it as GeoTIFF in QGIS (right-click on the layer › Export › Save As…).
erreurs.quand: A file is neither.

erreurs.message: <file>: give the circle's radius, in metres.
erreurs.quand: methode is moyenne or majorite without a positive rayon.

erreurs.message: <file>: a radius over 50 km isn't computed here.
erreurs.quand: rayon is over 50000.

erreurs.message: <file> has <n> band(s): give each one a name.
erreurs.quand: noms doesn't give one name per band.
