erreurs.message: The files joined under the name “<name>” must have the same method and radius.
erreurs.quand: Bands given the same name have different methods or radii.

erreurs.message: <file> is in <system>, and the project's coordinates are plane, without a stated system: choose their system in Plots › Map.
erreurs.quand: The raster has a system and the project's coordinates are "plan".

erreurs.message: <file> : <why the file is refused>
erreurs.quand: The file can't be read (damaged, a compression or a value type Nuée doesn't read, a coordinate system it doesn't convert…): raster.R's refusals, each naming the file.

ajouter_raster.effet_detail: One undo step (values from <files>), also noted as a data step, which Update the data replays: it keeps each raster file as the project keeps its source (its path, size, date and SHA-256). Each variable keeps where it came from (its files, bands, method, radius, system and cell size), which the Methods text says.

resumer_groupes.but: Summarizes a project into a new project of one observation per group of one or more columns (Edit › Summarize by group).

projet.description: The project to summarize, which doesn't change.

groupes.description: The columns that make the groups (the sector and the year…): variables by number, identifiers as "id:k". An observation without a value in one of them is left out, and counted.

variables.description: The quantitative variables to summarize; by default all of them but those of the groups.

statistiques.description: One or more statistics, each for every variable, in columns "<variable> (<statistic>)" named in the request's language; missing values are ignored.

valeurs.ecart_type: The standard deviation (missing for a single value).

resultat.description: The new project, named "<project> by <groups>" in the request's language: its observations the groups, named by their values, in the order of their columns; the group columns as they were (variables or identifiers); the qualitative variables and identifiers that don't vary within any group; the summaries.

resume.description: {groupes: the number of groups; observations: those summarized; sans_groupe: those left out for a missing group value; gardees: the qualitative variables and identifiers kept; laissees: those left out, as they vary within a group; phrase: that in a sentence}. One name alone in gardees or laissees comes as a string.

erreurs.message: Choose at least one column to make the groups
erreurs.quand: groupes is empty.

erreurs.message: Choose at least one statistic
erreurs.quand: statistiques is empty.

erreurs.message: Unknown statistic: <name>
erreurs.quand: A statistic isn't one of the values.

erreurs.message: “<name>” is qualitative: only quantitative variables are summarized (a qualitative variable is kept when it doesn't vary within a group)
erreurs.quand: variables names a qualitative variable.

erreurs.message: Choose at least one quantitative variable to summarize
erreurs.quand: No quantitative variable is left outside the groups.

erreurs.message: No observation has a value of <columns>
erreurs.quand: No observation has a value in every group column.

resumer_groupes.effet_detail: Opens the new project in the session, without a file and marked modified; like a pasted table, it has no data source, but its data steps start (Update the data, given a file). The project summarized doesn't change.

remplacer.but: Finds and replaces values in one, several or all variables, or previews what the replacement would change (Edit › Find and replace).

variables.description: The numbers of the variables to search; all of them without it.

chercher.description: The text or number to find; needed unless vides. A qualitative variable compares it as text (the whole cell, without the spaces around, or with partie a part of it); a quantitative one as a number on the whole cell ("3,5" is 3.5).

remplacer.description: What replaces it; empty, the cells become empty (missing). A quantitative variable takes only a number or nothing: with a text, its cells stay as they are, and are counted (ignorees).

vides.description: Find the empty cells (missing values) instead; chercher is then ignored.

partie.description: In a qualitative variable, replace chercher wherever it appears in the text ("," in "3,5"), as written; not with vides.

nombres.description: A qualitative variable whose values, once replaced, are all numbers becomes quantitative.

apercu.description: Only say what would change, changing nothing.

resultat.description: With apercu, an object with remplacement only; otherwise the project after the change, with remplacement.

remplacement.description: {cellules: the cells changed; variables: one per variable searched (always an array), each {variable, nom, cellules, ignorees: the cells left (a text for a quantitative variable), devient: quantitative, qualitative or "" when it stays what it was, categories_avant, categories_apres, exemples: the first changes, "a → b (n)", one alone as a string}; phrases: what changes, in sentences, one alone as a string}.

erreurs.message: Give the text or number to find, or find the empty cells.
erreurs.quand: chercher is empty without vides.

erreurs.message: No variable to search.
erreurs.quand: The project has no variable with data.

erreurs.message: No cell to replace.
erreurs.quand: Without apercu, no cell would change.

remplacer.effet_detail: With apercu nothing changes. Otherwise one undo step (replacement of <text>, or of empty cells), also noted as a data step, which Update the data replays; a category replaced by an existing one merges into it, one emptied disappears, and the project's model definitions follow the categories (atelier.R: suivre_categories).

categories.but: Renames, merges or reorders the categories of a qualitative variable (Edit › Categories).

noms.description: The new name of each of its categories, in their present order (Projet's categories): two given the same name merge into one. No name may be empty.

ordre.description: The order of the categories that result, by their names, each once; by default the order they come in (a merge takes the place of the first). In a regression, the last category observed is the reference.

resultat.description: The project after the change.

categories.description: {variable, nom, categories: the categories now (always an array), reference: the last, a regression's reference, phrases: what changed, in sentences}.

erreurs.message: <name> is quantitative: it has no categories.
erreurs.quand: The variable is quantitative.

erreurs.message: Give a name to each of the <n> categories of <name>.
erreurs.quand: noms doesn't give one name per category.

erreurs.message: A category can't have an empty name (Edit › Find and replace empties cells).
erreurs.quand: A name is empty.

erreurs.message: The order must give each category once: <categories>.
erreurs.quand: ordre doesn't give each resulting category once.

erreurs.message: The categories didn't change.
erreurs.quand: The names and order are those of now.

categories.effet_detail: One undo step (categories of <name>), also noted as a data step with the categories it renamed, which Update the data replays by their names; the observations keep their category under its new name, the project's model definitions follow, and a model of the session fitted with a category since renamed or merged must be fitted again before it refits or predicts (modele_perime).

decrire_variables.but: Sets the unit and the description of variables (Edit › Units and descriptions).

descriptions.description: One per variable, {variable: its number; unite: its unit, cut to 60 characters; description: cut to 1000}: a field absent or null stays as it is, an empty text removes it; line breaks and other control characters become spaces.

resultat.description: The project after the change (Projet's variables carry unite and description).

erreurs.message: No variable to describe.
erreurs.quand: descriptions is empty.

erreurs.message: The units and descriptions didn't change.
erreurs.quand: Every value given is the one already there.

decrire_variables.effet_detail: One undo step (units and descriptions), also noted as a data step, which Update the data replays on the variables the data still have.

renommer_variable.but: Renames a variable, the project's model definitions, the formulas of computed variables and the documents' references to its terms following, or previews what follows (in the Data view, a column header's right-click menu › Rename).

nom.description: The new name; line breaks and other control characters become spaces and the spaces around it are dropped. At most 200 characters, not starting with $, and neither another variable's name nor an identifier's of the observations.

apercu.description: true to only say what would follow the new name (renommage), changing nothing, or why it is refused, by the same errors: Rename's preview, asked as the name is typed.

resultat.description: With apercu, {renommage} only; otherwise the project after the change, with renommage.

renommage.description: {variable: its number; ancien, nom: its name before and now; modeles: the project's models whose definitions follow (their terms' names, their condition), R-code models aside; code: the R-code models that name it in their code, which isn't rewritten; formules: the computed variables whose formula follows; documents: the ids of the documents whose references follow (D1…); references: how many references follow; ajustes: the numbers of the project's models that a fit of the session made with the old name, to fit again so that their results take the new one; phrases: what it does, in sentences, in the request's language}; modeles, code, formules, documents, ajustes and phrases always arrays.

erreurs.message: Give the variable a name.
erreurs.quand: nom is left out, empty or only spaces.

erreurs.message: A variable's name has 200 characters at most.
erreurs.quand: nom is longer, once trimmed.

erreurs.message: The name didn't change.
erreurs.quand: nom is the variable's name now.

erreurs.message: A name that starts with $ is that of a model's scores as variables ($M1.t1): choose another one.
erreurs.quand: nom starts with $.

erreurs.message: A variable is already called “<name>”.
erreurs.quand: Another variable of the project has that name, capitals counting (unlike nom_variable_pris, the message ends with a full stop).

erreurs.message: “<name>” is the name of an identifier of the observations: a condition or a formula would no longer know which one it reads.
erreurs.quand: nom is the name of one of the observations' identifiers, the first included (Observation for a table).

renommer_variable.effet_detail: With apercu nothing changes. Otherwise one undo step (<old> renamed <new>, in the request's language), also noted as a data step that an update replays in its place: the variable takes the name; the project's model definitions follow (the names of their terms, their condition, a trend power's term, a forest's partial dependence), and so do the formulas of the computed variables that read it and the documents' references to its terms ({{M1.coef.site}}); an R-code model's code isn't rewritten. The session's fits keep their results under the old name, those whose condition came from their definition following it; refitting, predicting with or exporting one that used the variable is refused until it is fitted again from its definition. Edit › Undo takes it all back in one step, the references too, even in a document written since; Edit › Redo makes it again.

supprimer_variable.but: Deletes a variable and its values from a project, or previews what the deletion leaves (in the Data view, a column header's right-click menu › Delete).

apercu.description: true to only say what the deletion would leave (suppression), changing nothing; a refusal comes as the same error.

resultat.description: With apercu, {suppression} only; otherwise the project after the deletion, with suppression.

suppression.description: {variable: its number; nom: its name; code: the R-code models that name it in their code, to change there; formules: the computed variables whose formula reads it, which keep their values but can't be computed again; coordonnee: whether it was one of the project's coordinates, which it then no longer has; phrases: what it does, in sentences, in the request's language}; code, formules and phrases always arrays.

erreurs.message: It's the project's only variable: it can't be deleted.
erreurs.quand: The project's data have a single variable.

erreurs.message: <models> uses “<name>”: modify or delete it first (Model › Modify model).
erreurs.quand: A model of the project uses the variable (a term, its class, a curve, an offset, a random effect, its cross-validation groups, its settings) or names it in its condition; <models> their names ("M1, M2 and M3"). An R-code model doesn't stop it: phrases names it.

supprimer_variable.effet_detail: With apercu nothing changes. Otherwise one undo step (deletion of <name>, in the request's language), also noted as a data step that an update replays: the variable's column and values leave the data and the datasets, and the project's coordinates go when it was one of them; computed variables that read it keep their values. Edit › Undo brings it back in one step, Edit › Redo deletes it again.

type_variable.but: Treats a variable as categories or as numbers, the X terms of the project's model definitions following, or previews it (in the Data view, a column header's right-click menu › Treat as categories, or Treat as numbers).

valeurs.qualitative: categories: each distinct value one (a site coded 1, 2, 3), named by the number written to 15 significant digits, in increasing order
valeurs.quantitative: numbers: each category read as a number (3,5 or 3.5)

apercu.description: true to only say what the change would do (type), changing nothing; a refusal comes as the same error.

resultat.description: With apercu, {type} only; otherwise the project after the change, with type.

type.description: {variable: its number; nom: its name; type: qualitative or quantitative, as asked; categories: its categories now (empty as numbers); modeles: the project's models whose definitions follow; code: the R-code models that will see it otherwise when fitted again; phrases: what it does, in sentences, in the request's language}; categories, modeles, code and phrases always arrays.

erreurs.message: Unknown type: <type> (qualitative or quantitative).
erreurs.quand: type is left out, or is neither qualitative nor quantitative.

erreurs.message: “<name>” already is categories.
erreurs.quand: type is qualitative and the variable already is; likewise “<name>” already is numbers. for quantitative.

erreurs.message: <models> uses “<name>” otherwise than as an X variable (as Y, a class, a curve, a random effect, in its condition or its settings): modify it first (Model › Modify model).
erreurs.quand: A model of the project has the variable as a Y term, elsewhere than in its X terms, or in its condition; <models> their names ("M1 and M2").

erreurs.message: A qualitative variable enters a cross term once at most, neither squared nor cubed: "<term>".
erreurs.quand: As categories, when a model's X term has the variable twice (its square); <term> its variables' names joined by ×.

erreurs.message: These categories of “<name>” aren't numbers: “<category>”, …. Replace them first (Edit › Find and replace), or empty them.
erreurs.quand: As numbers, a category doesn't read as a number; the first five are named.

type_variable.effet_detail: With apercu nothing changes. Otherwise one undo step (<name> as categories, or <name> as numbers, in the request's language), also noted as a data step that an update replays. The X terms of the project's model definitions follow: one term per category, with the term's scaling, block and modifier and without its transformation, or a single term in numbers; a definition from a .usp file loses its stored solution. The session's fits keep their results, and refitting, predicting with or exporting one that used the variable is refused until it is fitted again from its definition. Edit › Undo takes it back in one step, Edit › Redo makes it again.

coordonnees.but: Gives the project's coordinates, a proposal made from its variables' names and the coordinate systems offered, and with regler sets or removes them.

regler.description: true sets the coordinates to x, y and systeme, or removes them without x.

x.description: With regler: the number of the variable holding x (the east, or the longitude); absent, the coordinates are removed.

y.description: With regler and x: the number of the variable holding y (the north, or the latitude).

systeme.description: With regler and x: their system, an EPSG code (2154, or "EPSG:2154") among those Nuée knows (WGS 84, ETRS89, RGF93, Lambert-93, CC42 to CC50, Lambert II étendu, LAEA Europe, web Mercator, UTM zones), or "plan" for plane coordinates in metres of an unstated system.

coordonnees.description: The coordinates set (after the change, with regler); null without.

proposition.description: Two quantitative variables whose names look like coordinates (longitude and latitude, X and Y, east and north…), {x, y, systeme: the system their values suggest, 4326, 2154, 27572 or "plan"}; null when none do.

systemes.description: The systems the interface lists, each {code, nom} (always an array).

projet.description: With regler, the project after the change; null otherwise.

erreurs.message: Unknown coordinate system: <code>
erreurs.quand: With regler, systeme isn't a system Nuée knows.

erreurs.message: Coordinates must be two different quantitative variables of the project.
erreurs.quand: With regler, x or y isn't a quantitative variable of the project, or they are the same.

erreurs.message: Longitudes and latitudes run from −180 to 180 and from −90 to 90: “<x>” or “<y>” goes beyond. Choose the system of the plane coordinates.
erreurs.quand: With regler, a longitude and latitude system for values beyond those bounds.

coordonnees.effet_detail: Only with regler: true, which sets the coordinates (or removes them) as one undo step (coordinates), also noted as a data step, which Update the data replays; without it nothing changes.

etapes.but: Gives the file a project's data came from, the changes made to them in Nuée since as steps that can be replayed, and whether the data are still those the file and the steps give (Edit › Data steps).

conformes.description: false leaves out conformes and raison, so that the data aren't read through for their fingerprint: the interface asks so when it only checks the source file (the status bar's notice).

source.description: The file the data came from, with three more fields: table, its sheet or table (null for none, and for a KoboToolbox or ODK import, whose settings name it); lecteur, how it is read again, tableau (a table, as File › Open reads it, with the decisions of its first reading on its columns), archive (a table of an ODK Central .zip opened as it is) or collecte (a KoboToolbox or ODK import, with its settings); formulaire, only for an import made with an XLSForm form, that form's FichierLu. null for a project without a source (a pasted table, a summary by group, imported spectra, a .usp project, the example, one from before 1.1): its steps are replayed only on a file given to mettre_a_jour.

etapes.description: Its steps, in the order they were made and are replayed (always an array, empty for none), each {n: its number from 1, retirer_etape's n; etiquette: what it does, written from its request and parameters in the request's language ("edit of yield (S1)", "sugar renamed brix"; "merge with Bob: …" for one a merge added; for a request this version doesn't know, the label noted with it); date: when it was made, local time, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss; demande: the request that made it, one of modifier_valeur, variable_calculee, imputer, classes_valeurs, ajouter_colonnes, ajouter_raster, remplacer, categories, coller_cellules, decrire_variables, renommer_variable, supprimer_variable, type_variable, coordonnees, classe_selection, baci_modele, scores_en_variables, kmeans_variable; fichiers: the files it read (an added table, a raster), each a FichierLu, always an array}.

conformes.description: Unless conformes is false: whether the data are still those the source and the steps give, by their fingerprint after the last step (etapes.R: donnees_conformes); false when they changed otherwise since (the R console, Nuée 1.0), null for a project without a fingerprint (from before 1.1, a .usp project, the example).

raison.description: Unless conformes is false: what to tell of conformes, in the request's language: for false, that updating the data would bring back those the source and the steps give; for null, that the project's changes from before 1.1 aren't steps; "" when the data conform.

etapes.effet_detail: No project changes; conformes is kept in a cache for the project's revision of its data (serveur.R: conformite_projet), so that asking again before they change doesn't read them all again.

mettre_a_jour.but: Updates a project's data from its source file read again, or from another file such as next year's, its data steps replayed on it, or previews what the update would change (Edit › Update the data).

chemin.description: The file to read; by default the project's source, found by its path from the folder of the project's file first, then by its absolute path. Needed for a project without a source, the file then read as File › Open reads a table (a KoboToolbox or ODK export by its import at the default settings); with a source, any file is read the source's way, with its decisions: the column that names the observations, the secondary identifiers, the columns read as numbers, or an import's settings and XLSForm form.

table.description: The sheet or table of the file to read (a workbook, an R file, a GeoPackage; the table of an ODK Central .zip opened as it is, by default the source's). For a table, by default the source's when the file has it or has no tables, else the file's only one: a file of several, none of them the source's, answers choisir. Ignored for a KoboToolbox or ODK import, whose settings name the table.

sans_nouvelles.description: The project's models that don't take the new observations the file brings, by their numbers (ResumeModele's numero) or names; the report's observations_choisies are those worth asking. By default each model takes those it admits.

apercu.description: true to only get the report of what the update would change, changing nothing.

resultat.description: With apercu, the report and apercu; otherwise the report and projet. When the file has several tables, none of them the source's, and table isn't given: {choisir, chemin} only, and nothing changes.

projet.description: Without apercu: the project after the update; its annulable is the update's label.

choisir.description: Instead of a report, the file's tables to choose from (always an array), to ask again with table.

chemin.description: With choisir: the file's absolute path, with / as separator.

erreurs.message: This project has no source file: give the file to read.
erreurs.quand: chemin is left out and the project has no source (etapes' source is null).

erreurs.message: Table not found in the file: <table>
erreurs.quand: table isn't one of an R file's tables; an unknown sheet of a workbook gets readxl's own Sheet '<table>' not found.

erreurs.message: <the reader's own message>
erreurs.quand: The file can't be read: R's or its package's message (readxl, haven…), untranslated, or one of ouvrir's refusals of an R file (R older than 4.4, an object Nuée doesn't open).

mettre_a_jour.effet_detail: With apercu, or a choisir answer, nothing changes. Otherwise one undo step (data update, in the request's language): the data become those of the file with the steps replayed, matched to the project as the report says (a variable keeps its number, name and categories, new categories going before the last; an observation keeps its number; new ones join, absent ones leave, the prediction sets too; a computed variable missing from the file is computed again from its formula); the model definitions follow (category codes, a term for each new category; the removed observations leave them, the new ones join those that admit them but the models of sans_nouvelles); the file read becomes the source (its relative path written again at the next save); every step stays, those skipped included; the data's fingerprint is renewed, so a change made outside the steps is gone. Documents, figures and the session's fits stay, the fits with the results of the data before until they are fitted again (the interface fits every model again, etapes.js). Edit › Undo gives back the data, the source and the steps in one step, and Edit › Redo makes the update again.

retirer_etape.but: Removes one of a project's data steps, its source file read again and the other steps replayed on it in place of its data, or previews what the removal would change (Edit › Data steps, Remove).

n.description: The step's number, as etapes gives it (n, from 1); a decimal is cut to its whole part.

apercu.description: true to only get the report of what the removal would change, changing nothing; the preview is made even when the source file changed since it was read, its new data then included.

table.description: The sheet or table of the source file to read when the source's own is no longer one of the file's (the answer without it is choisir), as for mettre_a_jour.

resultat.description: The report of the data that the source and the other steps give, compared to the project's (its etapes numbered without the step removed): with apercu, the report and apercu; otherwise the report and projet. When the source file has several tables, none of them the source's, and table isn't given: {choisir, chemin} only, and nothing changes.

projet.description: Without apercu: the project after the removal; its annulable is the removal's label.

choisir.description: Instead of a report, the file's tables to choose from (always an array), to ask again with table.

chemin.description: With choisir: the file's absolute path, with / as separator.

erreurs.message: Unknown step: <n>
erreurs.quand: n is left out, isn't a number, or is below 1 or above the number of the project's steps.

erreurs.message: This project has no source file: its steps can't be redone without it.
erreurs.quand: The project has no source (etapes' source is null): a pasted table, a summary by group, imported spectra, a .usp project, the example, one from before 1.1.

erreurs.message: The source file changed since it was read: removing the step would also bring in its new data. Update the data first, or look at the removal's preview.
erreurs.quand: Without apercu, the source file changed since it was read (etapes' source.modifie): its size, or its date and its content. Besides erreur, the answer carries source_modifiee: true.

erreurs.message: The file <file>, read by a step or by the import, changed since it was read: removing the step would also bring in its new data. Update the data first, or look at the removal's preview.
erreurs.quand: Without apercu, the import's XLSForm form or a file one of the remaining steps reads (joined columns, a raster) changed since it was read. Besides erreur, the answer carries source_modifiee: true.

erreurs.message: Table not found in the file: <table>
erreurs.quand: table isn't one of an R file's tables; an unknown sheet of a workbook gets readxl's own Sheet '<table>' not found.

erreurs.message: <the reader's own message>
erreurs.quand: The source file can't be read (with apercu, as it is now): R's or its package's message, untranslated.

retirer_etape.effet_detail: With apercu, or a choisir answer, nothing changes. Otherwise one undo step (removal of step <n>, in the request's language): the data become those the source file, read again, and the other steps give, matched to the project and its model definitions following as mettre_a_jour does it; the step leaves the list, those after it moving up one number, the source's state is renewed, and a change made outside the steps (conformes false) is gone. The session's fits keep their results until they are fitted again (the interface fits every model again, etapes.js). Edit › Undo gives back the data, the source and the steps, the step removed included, in one step; Edit › Redo removes it again.

fichier_change.but: Says whether an open project's file was changed on disk since the project read or saved it (a colleague saving it on a shared folder), and by whom when the file says.

resultat.description: For a project the engine never read from a project file nor saved to one (a table opened or pasted, imported spectra…; an example project knows its file of exemple/): {change: false, connu: false, existe: false, base: false}. Otherwise its file's size and date compared with those known, then, when they differ, its content (a date alone changed, the content the same, isn't a change); the interface asks every 30 seconds (versions.js: surveillerDossiers).

change.description: Whether the file's content is no longer what the project read or last saved; false when the file no longer exists.

connu.description: Whether the engine knows a file of the project: a .nuee or .json it was opened from, a file it was saved to, or the file of a recovery copy reopened with its lu.

existe.description: Whether that file exists now (false: deleted, moved or renamed).

chemin.description: That file, its absolute path with / as separator; absent when connu is false.

base.description: Whether the session keeps a copy of the file as the project read or last saved it, so that fusionner with projet can merge their changes (none for a project reopened from a recovery copy, as after a restart of the engine, for an old version or a hidden project, or when the copy couldn't be written).

taille.description: Its size now, in bytes; absent when it doesn't exist.

date.description: Its modification time now, in the engine's local time, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss (not seconds since 1970, as EtatFichier and Save's 409 give it); absent when it doesn't exist.

auteur.description: With change, who saved it, when the file says (enregistrer's auteur, written in its nuee); absent otherwise.

version.description: With change, the version of Nuée that saved it, when the file says; absent otherwise.

fichier_change.effet_detail: No project's content changes. When the file's size or date changed but not its content (a sync program touched it, it was copied back), the size and date the engine keeps of the file become its own, so that Save doesn't ask before writing over it; the first comparison of contents also keeps the fingerprint of the copy compared with.

fusionner.but: Prepares the merge of two versions of a project by meaning, from the last version both had, and says what clashes and what each side brought, without changing anything yet.

projet.description: My side as the session's project, as it is now, its unsaved changes included (a project on a shared folder: Save's 409 answer says fusion when this is possible). Without base, the base is the copy of its file the session kept when the project read or last saved it; without leur, their side is that file as it is now on disk (someone else may have saved it since). With projet, their side is copied into the engine's temporary folder first, and read from the copy. An old version opened read-only, or a project the interface doesn't show (ouvrir's lecture_seule, cache), is refused.

mien.description: Without projet, my side: a project file (.nuee, .json), required then. Ignored with projet.

base.description: The version both sides last had, a project file (for a project shared with GitHub or GitLab, the two histories' common version: interface/versions.js). Required without projet; with projet, the copy of its file kept in the session by default.

leur.description: Their side, a project file. Required without projet; with projet, the project's own file by default (the one it was read from or last saved to).

dossier.description: The folder from which the data's source and the steps' files are found, by their path from it first, then by their absolute path (etapes.R: fichier_retrouve), for a merge by steps; by default the project's folder with projet, else the folder of mien.

resultat.description: The merge as fusion.R's fusionner_projets makes it with no choice yet, what the interface's merge dialog shows (versions.js: contenuFusion); nothing is merged until fusionner_finir.

fusion.description: The prepared merge's id (fusion1, fusion2…): fusionner_finir's fusion.

auto.description: true when nothing clashes: fusionner_finir needs no choice.

conflits.description: The clashes, each needing a choice in fusionner_finir's choix, in the order the merge meets them (the data, coordinates and prediction sets, then models, documents, figures and the project's other fields); always an array, empty when auto.

apports.description: What each side changed since the base, {mien, leur}, each an array of sentences in the request's language (always arrays): models, documents and figures added, removed or changed (a model's changes in a few words, "M3: 2 component(s) → 4 component(s); X: + x5", four at most, then how many more), their model renamed when both sides made one of the same name, the data updated from a file, the steps added, variables and observations added or removed, cells changed, new categories, units, descriptions or formulas.

donnees.description: How the data were merged, {mode, raison}: mode "inchangees" (neither side changed them), "etapes" (both sides only added steps to the base's: replayed from the data's source, read again, so that the data stay what their steps give) or "cellules" (cell by cell, the variables by their names, the observations by their identifiers); raison, with cellules, why not by steps when it is worth saying ("data changed outside the steps", "steps of the base were removed", "the source <file> isn't found on this computer", "the source has several tables", "the step “<step>” no longer applies after the others (<why>)", or the replay's own error), else "" (also for projects without a data source, such as those of Nuée 1.0).

qui.description: Their side, for the sentences: who saved their file, when the file says (enregistrer's auteur, written in its nuee), else that file's name ("partage.nuee").

notes.description: What to know of the merge, in the request's language: a variable merged as quantitative whose text values from one side were left empty (always an array).

erreurs.message: This old version is read-only: it isn't merged.
erreurs.quand: projet is an old version opened read-only, or a project the interface doesn't show (ouvrir's lecture_seule or cache).

erreurs.message: My side is missing: q$mien (a file) or q$projet.
erreurs.quand: Neither projet nor mien is given (the interface asks fusionner without parameters once, to know whether the engine merges: any answer but Unknown request says it does).

erreurs.message: No common version to merge from: this project was neither opened from a file nor saved since Nuée started.
erreurs.quand: There is no base: base isn't given and projet keeps no copy of its file (it was never opened from a .nuee or .json nor saved since the engine started, it was reopened from a recovery copy, or the copy couldn't be written), or base or that copy isn't an existing file. Without projet, a base missing or not found gets this message too.

erreurs.message: Not a Nuée project (.nuee): <file name>
erreurs.quand: base, mien or leur isn't a .nuee or .json file (with projet, leur is read from its copy, named .nuee: another kind of file gets jsonlite's own message instead).

erreurs.message: <jsonlite's own message>
erreurs.quand: A file that isn't a project's JSON, untranslated.

fusionner.effet_detail: No project changes. The prepared merge is kept in the session under its id until fusionner_finir uses it (the last five prepared are kept: a sixth drops the oldest); with projet, the copy of their file it read is kept with it, in the engine's temporary folder.

fusionner_finir.but: Finishes a merge prepared by fusionner with the side chosen for each clash: the merged project takes the place of the session's project as one undo step, or a merge of three files is written to a file.

fusion.description: The prepared merge's id (fusionner's fusion). Its project is the one it was prepared with: a projet sent with it is ignored.

choix.description: The side chosen for each clash, by its id: {"<Conflit's id>": "mien" | "leur"}, mien keeping what my side made of what clashes, leur taking theirs; one for every clash, any other value counting as none. The merge is made again with these choices.

chemin.description: Where to write the merged project (a .nuee). For a merge of three files, without it <my side's project name>.nuee (fusion.nuee without a name) in a new folder of the engine's temporary folder, for a browser to fetch with /api/fichier; its relative paths are written from fusionner's dossier. For a merge prepared with projet, the merged project is also written there once it has taken the project's place, its relative paths from the project's folder; the project still counts as modified and keeps the state it knew of its file, so that when chemin is the project's own file, the next save over it asks first (409).

version.description: Nuée's version, written in the file with R's and the packages', when a file is written.

auteur.description: Who merges, written in the file as enregistrer writes it (its nuee.auteur, which fichier_change and fusionner give as auteur and qui): a name, or {nom, email} of which only nom is written; none without it.

resultat.description: A merge of three files (fusionner without projet): {chemin}. A merge prepared with projet: {projet, etiquette, documents}, with chemin too when chemin was given.

chemin.description: The file written.

projet.description: The merged project, under the same id: modified, its annulable the merge's label.

etiquette.description: The label of its undo step, "merge with <qui>" (fusionner's qui), in the request's language.

documents.description: For a merge prepared with projet: the ids of the project's documents whose text the merge changed, for a client to read them again in the editors it has open (always an array).

erreurs.message: Unknown merge: <id>
erreurs.quand: fusion isn't a merge prepared in this session and not yet finished: finished already, dropped (only the last five prepared are kept), or prepared before the engine restarted.

erreurs.message: Choose mine or theirs for: <titles>
erreurs.quand: choix doesn't give mien or leur for every clash of the merge made again; <titles> are those clashes' titles, separated by commas.

erreurs.message: Unknown project: <id>
erreurs.quand: The project the merge was prepared with (fusionner's projet) was closed since.

erreurs.message: The project changed since the merge was prepared: it must be done again.
erreurs.quand: A merge prepared with projet, and the project changed since fusionner (in anything but its unsaved state and what fichier_change keeps of its file).

erreurs.message: <R's own message>
erreurs.quand: The file can't be written, its folder missing for instance ("cannot open the connection", untranslated). With projet, the merge has already taken the project's place, its undo step kept, when chemin fails.

fusionner_finir.effet_detail: A merge prepared with projet: the merged project takes the place of the session's project under the same id (its name, its file and the interface's session it holds stay mine), counts as modified, and the session's models whose observations came from a condition of the project follow its merged condition; when their side was the project's own file, the project counts as having read that file as fusionner found it, so that Save writes over it without asking. That is one undo step, "merge with <qui>": Edit › Undo (annuler) gives the project back as it was before, with the documents, figures and file state it had when they haven't changed since the merge (the file is then seen changed again, and can be merged again), Edit › Redo (retablir) merges it again, and a new change empties Redo. A merge of three files changes no project and leaves nothing to undo: it only writes the merged project. Either way the prepared merge is used up.

verifier.but: Checks a model's data before it is fitted: the variables and observations with more than half of their values missing, and the constant variables.

resultat.description: Only the problems; TRIM and DISTANCE check their own data when fitted, and an R-code or plugin model has its code do it: they give two empty tables written {}.

variables.description: A table of the variables that have more than half of their values missing or are constant: uid, nom, manquantes (the share missing, from 0 to 1, of its worst term), constante; its columns are empty arrays when there is none.

observations.description: A table of the observations that miss more than half of their X values: uid, nom, manquantes (a share, from 0 to 1).

erreurs.quand: exclues and test leave the model no observation.

erreurs.message: An OPLS needs at least one Y variable
erreurs.quand: An OPLS without y; an OPLS-DA with fewer than two classes gets "An OPLS-DA needs at least two classes", a PLS-DA with a single class "A PLS-DA needs at least two classes".

erreurs.message: Choose at least one X variable.
erreurs.quand: A PCA, PLS or OPLS (or PLS-DA, OPLS-DA) without x.

erreurs.message: Unknown spectral preprocessing: <type>
erreurs.quand: A step of spectres isn't snv, msc, sg, detrend or ligne_base.

erreurs.message: Unknown cross-validation: <validation> (sans_fuite, centres or complet).
erreurs.quand: validation is neither empty nor one of its values.

erreurs.message: Cross-validation: this project has no ID "<id>".
erreurs.quand: vc names an identifier the project hasn't.

erreurs.message: Unknown grouping "<by>"
erreurs.quand: A random effect's or the CAR1 time's by is neither id nor variable.

erreurs.message: “<name>” has values too large for the computation< (up to <value>)>: their squares exceed the numbers R can hold. Divide it by a power of 10 (Edit › New variable).
erreurs.quand: A UV or Pareto term has values beyond about 1e150 in size, or infinite ones; values all below 1e-150 get "“<name>” has values too small for the computation (at most <value>): their squares vanish. Multiply it by a power of 10 (Edit › New variable)."

erreurs.message: Write the model's R code: its last value is the fitted model.
erreurs.quand: An R-code model (CODE) whose options' code is left out or blank.

erreurs.message: <a plugin definition's refusal>
erreurs.quand: A plugin's model (PLUGIN) whose definition its plugin refuses, in the engine's words: no options' greffon.id (Which plugin? The definition names none (options$greffon$id).), a plugin not installed, a version neither installed nor in the project, a plugin with errors or that needs a newer Nuée, an unknown input or option, a variable an input doesn't accept, too few or too many variables, an option's value of another type or out of its bounds (greffons.R: definir_plugin).

condition_observations.but: Counts the ticked observations that a model's condition keeps, for New model's Observations tab.

condition.description: The condition, an R expression read without running anything (condition.R: lire_condition); empty or absent, every ticked observation counts.

exclues.description: The unticked observations' numbers, not counted.

test.description: The test set's observations, not counted either.

n.description: The ticked observations where the condition is true (a missing value counts as false).

total.description: The ticked observations: all of the project's, less exclues and test.

erreurs.message: Variable not found: <name> (check the name; a name with spaces or signs is written between `backticks`)
erreurs.quand: The condition names a variable or identifier the project hasn't.

erreurs.message: Unreadable condition: <R's message>
erreurs.quand: The text isn't R.

erreurs.message: A condition is a single expression, without ";": site == "S1" & year >= 2010.
erreurs.quand: Several expressions.

erreurs.message: This condition is too long.
erreurs.quand: More than 5000 characters.

erreurs.message: In a condition, ":" only goes between two numbers, like year %in% 2005:2010.
erreurs.quand: A range whose bounds aren't numbers.

erreurs.message: This ":" range is too long (more than 100000 values).
erreurs.quand: A range of more than 100,000 values.

erreurs.message: Incomplete condition: an argument is missing.
erreurs.quand: An empty argument, c(1, , 2).

erreurs.message: "<expression>" has no place in a condition.
erreurs.quand: Something that is neither a call, a name nor a constant.

erreurs.message: Condition: <R's message>
erreurs.quand: Evaluating it failed.

erreurs.message: The condition must give TRUE or FALSE (or 1 and 0) for each observation; it gives text.
erreurs.quand: It gives text; likewise "; it gives other numbers (<number>)." and "; it gives <class>.".

erreurs.message: The condition must give one value per observation (<n>); it gives <m>.

jeu_test.but: Proposes a test set: a share of the observations, drawn at random or chosen by Kennard–Stone, by class when a class variable is given.

methode.description: How the test set is chosen.

valeurs.hasard: at random, from R's random numbers without a seed: two calls give two sets
valeurs.kennard_stone: Kennard and Stone (1969): the model keeps the observations that cover the data, on the quantitative x, centred and scaled

x.description: kennard_stone: the X variables whose quantitative ones it works on.

part.description: The share of the observations (of each class) set aside.

classe.description: A variable whose classes each give their share (a class too small to give one observation and keep two gives none).

exclues.description: Observations left out of the choice (the unticked ones).

test.description: The test set's observations, their numbers in increasing order (always an array).

erreurs.message: "<methode>" isn't a choice of test set method: hasard, kennard_stone.
erreurs.quand: methode is another value.

formule.but: Writes the R formula of a regression's settings, as lm, mgcv and lme4 write it.

resultat.description: Only type (LM when absent), x, y, transformations, croises, lisses, k_courbes, par_courbes, aleatoires, decalage and lisse_spatial count.

formule.description: The formula, "weight ~ log10(diameter) + s(firmness) + (1 | orchard)"; without y, "~ x1 + x2"; without x, "y ~ 1".

erreurs.message: Logit: the lower bound (<C1>) must be smaller than the upper bound (<C2>).
erreurs.quand: A logit transformation whose bounds are in the wrong order.

erreurs.message: Unknown grouping "<by>"
erreurs.quand: A random effect's by is neither id nor variable.

lire_formule.but: Reads an R formula into a regression's settings, without ever evaluating it.

texte.description: The formula: response ~ terms, with the project's variables and identifiers, numbers, log, log10, log1p, exp, sqrt, I(), s(), offset(log()), random effects as lme4 writes them, ":" and "*".

type.description: The regression's type so far (LM, LMM, GLM or GAM; another value is LM): random effects make an LM mixed and their absence an LMM linear, a curve or a spatial smooth makes it a GAM.

famille.description: The distribution so far: an offset needs a log-link one.

resultat.description: The settings, in the form of the definition parameters.

type.description: The regression's type the formula gives.

x.description: The X variables' numbers (always an array).

y.description: The response's number, in an array.

croises.description: The cross terms and powers (always an array).

lisses.description: The variables in a curve (always an array).

k_courbes.description: By variable number, a curve's k.

par_courbes.description: By variable number, the qualitative variable of a curve per category.

aleatoires.description: The random effects, the widest first (always an array).

ajuster.but: Fits a model, from its definition or from a model kept in the project, and keeps it in the session.

numero.description: A model of the project, by its number (ResumeModele's numero) or its name: it is fitted as the project keeps it, and the definition parameters are ignored but A, which replaces its number of components when above 0. Without numero, the definition parameters make the model.
