erreurs.quand: A plugin's model (PLUGIN) whose definition its plugin refuses, in the engine's words: no options' greffon.id (Which plugin? The definition names none (options$greffon$id).), a plugin not installed, a version neither installed nor in the project, a plugin with errors or that needs a newer Nuée, an unknown input or option, a variable an input doesn't accept, too few or too many variables, an option's value of another type or out of its bounds (greffons.R: definir_plugin).

erreurs.message: `valeurs`: named numbers, such as c(density = 3.2, slope = -0.4).
erreurs.quand: An R-code or plugin model's code returned a list whose valeurs or tableaux aren't what they must be: numbers without a name, names that repeat (Names of `valeurs` repeat: <names>.), tableaux that aren't named data.frames (`tableaux`: named data.frames, such as list(counts = d).).

ajuster.effet_detail: The fitted model joins the session under a new id. A definition made by Nuée joins the project, replacing the one of the same name: sent without numero, under a new number; with numero, under its own. The project counts as modified when the definition changed (refitting a saved model leaves it as it was), and a definition added or changed empties the redo stack (retablir), but not one fitted again by its number. A definition sent with meme_numero takes the place of the project's model of that number, whatever its name. A model read from a .usp file only joins the session.

reajuster.but: Fits a fitted model again with a change: observations left out, another number of components, the terms kept by the VIP, a model of its AIC selection, a CAR1 autocorrelation or a quantitative X variable centred.

exclues.description: Observations to leave out, by their numbers, besides those the model already leaves out.

A.description: PCA and PLS: the number of components; without it, 0 (the automatic fit) when exclues or garder is given, else the model's.

garder.description: PCA and PLS: the names of the X terms to keep (the VIP's), with the factors of their cross terms.

groupes_aic.description: Regressions: the groups of terms of a model of the AIC selection (selection_aic's groupes), the terms kept (Fit this model).

car1.description: Regressions with random effects: {temps: a Groupement, the time; groupe: {by: "effets"}, its random effects' groups, optionally followed by a finer level's Groupement}: the same model with a CAR1 autocorrelation (Fit with CAR1).

centrer.description: Regressions: the numbers of quantitative X variables, terms of the model on their own, centred on their mean (their scaling becomes Ctr; their cross terms keep theirs), as the model's checks propose (Fit again with “<name>” centred).

resultat.description: The new model, named "<name> (<n>)".

erreurs.message: A regression has no VIP.
erreurs.quand: garder for a regression; another analysis gets "This analysis has no VIP.".

erreurs.message: Unknown group of terms in this model: <names>
erreurs.quand: groupes_aic names a group the model hasn't.

erreurs.message: This model has no random effect: a CAR1 autocorrelation works within the groups of a random effect.
erreurs.quand: car1 for a model without random effects.

erreurs.message: This model already has a CAR1 autocorrelation.
erreurs.quand: car1 for a model with one.

erreurs.message: Choose the time (a year, a day...): an ID or a quantitative variable.
erreurs.quand: car1 without temps.

erreurs.message: A CAR1 autocorrelation works within the groups of the model's random effects, or of a finer level within them: choose its random effects as the groups.
erreurs.quand: car1's groupe doesn't start with {by: "effets"}, or has more than one finer level.

erreurs.message: Autocorrelation in time needs a single time per group: several observations have the same time in the same group.
erreurs.quand: The CAR1 time repeats within a group.

erreurs.message: This variable isn't a quantitative X variable of the model.
erreurs.quand: centrer names no quantitative X variable that is a term of the model on its own.

erreurs.message: None of the terms to keep is an X term of the model.
erreurs.quand: garder names none of the model's X terms.

erreurs.message: No observation is ticked for this model: tick some in the Observations tab (those of the test set aren't part of it).
erreurs.quand: exclues leaves the model no observation.

erreurs.message: The response “<name>” is <value> for each of the model's <n> observations: there is nothing to explain. Choose another response, or other observations.
erreurs.quand: The response of a regression (a regression tree, a forest, boosted trees) has a single value over the observations left.

erreurs.message: `valeurs`: named numbers, such as c(density = 3.2, slope = -0.4).
erreurs.quand: An R-code or plugin model's code returned a list whose valeurs or tableaux aren't what they must be: numbers without a name, names that repeat (Names of `valeurs` repeat: <names>.), tableaux that aren't named data.frames (`tableaux`: named data.frames, such as list(counts = d).).

reajuster.effet_detail: The refitted model joins the session, and its definition, named "<name> (<n>)" with a new number, the project, which counts as modified.

supprimer_modele.but: Removes a fitted model from the session, and with definition its definition from the project.

definition.description: true to also remove its definition (every one of its name) from the project.

supprime.description: The id of the model removed.

supprimer_modele.effet_detail: Without definition, the fitted model only leaves the session (other fits of the same definition stay). With definition: true, the definition leaves the project too, which counts as modified, with one undo step.

note_modele.but: Sets a fitted model's free note, kept with its definition in the project.
note_modele.effet_detail: The note is kept with the fitted model and with every definition of its name in the project, which counts as modified when the note changed.

modeles_classe.but: Fits class models: a PCA for each category of a class variable, on that class's observations.

classe.description: The qualitative variable whose categories are the classes; it replaces the definition's classe, and the type is always PCA.

modeles.description: A model per class with three observations or more, named "<nom>.<class>", their groupe the name nom and their classe_modele the class (always an array).

erreurs.message: Class models need a class variable (Class role).
erreurs.quand: classe is missing.

erreurs.message: The class variable must be qualitative
erreurs.quand: classe is a quantitative variable.

erreurs.message: No class has enough observations (3 or more)
erreurs.quand: Every class has fewer than three observations.

erreurs.message: No observation is ticked for this model: tick some in the Observations tab (those of the test set aren't part of it).
erreurs.quand: exclues and test leave no observation.

erreurs.message: Choose at least one X variable.
erreurs.quand: x is empty.

erreurs.message: Unknown cross-validation: <validation> (sans_fuite, centres or complet).
erreurs.quand: validation is neither empty nor one of its values.

erreurs.message: “<name>” has values too large for the computation< (up to <value>)>: their squares exceed the numbers R can hold. Divide it by a power of 10 (Edit › New variable).
erreurs.quand: A UV or Pareto term has values beyond about 1e150 in size, or infinite ones; values all below 1e-150 get "“<name>” has values too small for the computation (at most <value>): their squares vanish. Multiply it by a power of 10 (Edit › New variable)."

modeles_classe.effet_detail: Each class model joins the session, and its definition the project, which counts as modified.

par_reponse.but: Fits a regression again for each of several responses and sets their coefficients, tests and quality side by side.

modele.description: The fitted regression's id: its terms, random effects, distribution, curves and observations are kept, its response's transformation applied to each.

reponses.description: The responses' variable numbers (quantitative, none of the model's X).

correction.description: The correction of each term's p over the responses.

garder.description: Also keep each response's model in the session and the project.

tableau.description: A table, one row per term and response, terme by terme: reponse, terme, estimation, erreur_type, bas, haut, p, edf (a curve's), p_corrige; null when no response could be fitted.

resume.description: A table, one row per response: reponse, N, AIC, R2, Q2, erreur ("" when fitted, else why it couldn't be: a response that fails isn't an error of the request).

effets.description: For each response fitted, {reponse, effets}: its terms' effect curves, as effets gives them.

methodes.description: The Methods sentence, in the request's language.

erreurs.message: One model per response is made from a regression (LM, LMM, GLM or GAM).
erreurs.quand: The model isn't a regression.

erreurs.message: Choose at least one response.
erreurs.quand: reponses is empty.

erreurs.message: An X variable can't also be a response: <names>.
erreurs.quand: A response is one of the model's X.

erreurs.message: "<correction>" isn't a choice of p-value correction: BH, holm, bonferroni.
erreurs.quand: correction is another value.

par_reponse.effet_detail: Only with garder: each response's model that was fitted joins the session, and its definition, named "<name> · <response>", the project, which counts as modified; without garder nothing is kept.

baci_modele.but: Fits the BACI mixed model, y ~ period × impact + (1 | unit) with CAR1 if asked, adding its two 0/1 variables to the project when they don't exist yet.

temps.description: The time: a variable or "id:k" (k ≥ 2) of numbers (the year) or dates.

unite.description: The unit (the site or sector): a qualitative variable or "id:k" (k ≥ 2).

impact.description: The impact units: categories of unite.

temoins.description: The control units: other categories of unite.

evenement.description: The first time counted after: a number, or a date when the time is made of dates.

fin.description: The last time of the after period, included; the later times are left out.

car1.description: With a CAR1 autocorrelation along the time within each unit (a single row per unit and time).

modele.description: The model, named "BACI <y>" (the model of the same settings is replaced, keeping its name and number; another takes "BACI <y> (2)"…).

variables.description: The names of the period and impact variables, "BACI period (2008)" and "BACI impact (S1 vs S2, S3)" (always an array).

nouvelles.description: Those of them just added to the project (always an array, empty when both existed with these values).

erreurs.message: Enter the event, the first time counted as “after”: the mixed model compares the two periods.
erreurs.quand: No evenement.

erreurs.message: The response, the time and the unit must be three different variables
erreurs.quand: Two of y, temps and unite are the same.

erreurs.message: The response must be a quantitative variable
erreurs.quand: y is qualitative.

erreurs.message: The time (<name>) must be numbers (the year) or dates (2019-05-14, 14/05/2019): <why>
erreurs.quand: A value of the time is neither a number nor a date (", not both" for a mix).

erreurs.message: The unit must be a qualitative variable or an ID
erreurs.quand: unite is quantitative.

erreurs.message: Choose at least one impact unit and one control unit
erreurs.quand: impact or temoins is empty.

erreurs.message: <unit> has no level <levels>
erreurs.quand: impact or temoins names a category unite hasn't.

erreurs.message: A unit can't be both impact and control: <units>
erreurs.quand: A unit in both.

erreurs.message: No value of <time> where both the impact and the controls have a value of <y>
erreurs.quand: The impact and the controls share no time.

erreurs.message: “<y>” has values too large for the computation< (up to <value>)>: their squares exceed the numbers R can hold. Divide it by a power of 10 (Edit › New variable).
erreurs.quand: y has values beyond about 1e150 in size, or infinite ones, on the rows compared; values all below 1e-150 get "“<y>” has values too small for the computation (at most <value>): their squares vanish. Multiply it by a power of 10 (Edit › New variable)."

erreurs.message: The event time must be a number or a date
erreurs.quand: evenement can't be read (fin: "The end of the after period must be a number or a date").

erreurs.message: The end of the after period (<end>) comes before the event (<event>)
erreurs.quand: fin before evenement.

erreurs.message: At least two values of <time> are needed in each period, before and after <event>: there are <n> before and <m> after
erreurs.quand: A period with fewer than two times.

erreurs.message: The gap is the same at every time: nothing to compare
erreurs.quand: The impact − control gap never varies.

erreurs.message: Several rows of the same unit at the same time (<units>): CAR1 autocorrelation needs a single time per unit. Fit the model without CAR1, or choose a finer unit (the sector rather than the site).
erreurs.quand: car1 with repeated times in a unit.

baci_modele.effet_detail: The two 0/1 variables, when they don't exist yet with these values, are added to the project as one undo step (variable <names>), which annuler takes back with the model's definition, and noted as a data step (BACI variables), which Update the data replays; the model joins the session and its definition the project. Reusing existing variables leaves no undo step.

empreinte_code.but: Gives the fingerprint of an R code, which code_approuve takes to approve it (New model asks it before fitting the code just written).

code.description:
The R code, as an R-code model's definition holds it (its options' code): its text in UTF-8, its 
 and  line ends counting as 
 (a code pasted from Windows has the fingerprint of the same code typed); an array is its lines, joined with 
.

empreinte.description: Its SHA-256, 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, the same whatever the R (code.R's sha256_r on an R older than 4.5, which has no tools::sha256sum): what code_approuve takes, and ResumeModele's code_r.empreinte for the same code.

code_approuve.but: Gives the engine the fingerprints of the R-code models' and plugins' code this user approved on this computer, the only such code it runs.

empreintes.description: The fingerprints approved (empreinte_code's, ResumeModele's code_r.empreinte, a plugin's), each 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters; any other value is left out, without an error. From the application (the engine started with a secret, the request carrying it in the header X-Nuee-Code), the whole list it keeps (the latest 10,000), which replaces the engine's; to an engine started by hand, those to add. Without it, none: with a secret, every approval is withdrawn.

n.description: The number of fingerprints the engine now holds approved.

erreurs.message: Only the application approves R code (Run it, in the bar above the project).
erreurs.quand: The engine was started with a secret (NUEE_CODE_SECRET in its environment: the application draws one at each start, and the engine removes it from its environment once read) and the request doesn't carry it in the header X-Nuee-Code: the windows, which have the token but not the secret, can't approve code themselves. The answer is HTTP 403, given before the parameters are read; nothing changes.

code_approuve.effet_detail: The fingerprints the engine holds approved, for as long as it runs: with a secret, exactly those given; without one, those given added to them. An R-code model (type CODE) or a plugin runs only when its fingerprint is among them (ajuster, reajuster, script_r and the replays of Update the data refuse the others), and ResumeModele's code_r.approuve and code_modeles' approuve say whether it is. No project changes.

code_modeles.but: Gives the code of a project's R-code models, with each one's fingerprint and whether it is approved on this computer, to read before running it (Show the code, in the bar above the project).

modeles.description: One per R-code model (type CODE) of the project, in its order, each {nom, numero (ResumeModele's numero, null without one), titre, code (as the engine keeps and runs it: UTF-8, \n line ends), empreinte (its fingerprint, as empreinte_code gives it), approuve (whether its fingerprint is among the approved ones)}; always an array, empty without such a model. A plugin's models aren't listed.

greffons.but: Lists the plugins of the user's and of the organisation's plugins folders, as File › Plugins… shows them, with those folders and whether plugins can be installed here.

resultat.description: What the interface knows of the plugins (greffons.R: greffons_interface); etat gives the same in its field greffons.

dossier.description: The user's plugins folder, where greffon_installer writes (NUEE_GREFFONS: the desktop application gives <userData>/greffons); null without it, an engine started by hand.

organisation.description: The organisation's plugins folder, read only (NUEE_GREFFONS_ORGANISATION: the PluginsFolder policy); null without one.

interdit.description: Whether the DisableCustomCode policy is on (NUEE_SANS_CODE=1): only the organisation's plugins run, and none installs.

installation.description: Whether plugins can be installed here: a user's plugins folder, and the policy off.

liste.description: The plugins of both folders, the organisation's first, one per sub-folder whose name doesn't start with a dot (one that can't be read too, invalide with its error), without their files (always an array).

greffon_lire.but: Reads a plugin from a file without running anything, before it is installed: its manifest, its code, its errors, whether it can be installed, and the installed version of the same id.

chemin.description: A .nueeplugin (a zip archive with plugin.json at its root or in its single folder), the plugin.json of a plugin's folder, or that folder (File › Plugins… › Show reads an installed one's folder this way).

resultat.description: What the install dialog shows (greffons.R: installation_greffon).

greffon.description: The plugin read, source fichier, with its fichiers: plugin.json, then the R files its manifest lists (every .R file read when the manifest has errors).

raison.description: Why it can't, in the request's language, the first that applies (greffon_installer's refusals: it has errors; the DisableCustomCode policy; no user's plugins folder; the organisation already gives that id; it needs a newer Nuée); "" when it can.

installe.description: The valid plugin of the same id already in a plugins folder, the organisation's first: {version, empreinte, source (utilisateur or organisation), ordre (1 when the one read is newer, -1 older, 0 the same version; null when either has no version), meme (whether they are the same files, the same fingerprint)}; null when there is none.

greffon_lire.effet_detail: Nothing runs: the manifest is read and the R files only parsed. A .nueeplugin is unpacked (its plugin.json and .R files) into a temporary folder, deleted after.

greffon_installer.but: Installs a plugin read from a file, or carried by a model of a project, into the user's plugins folder, in place of the version of the same id.

chemin.description: The plugin's file, as greffon_lire takes it (a .nueeplugin, a plugin.json, a plugin's folder); required unless projet and numero are given.

projet.description: Without chemin: the project whose model carries the plugin (Install and run, in the bar above the project).

numero.description: With projet: that model, by its number (ResumeModele's numero) or its name.

empreinte.description: The fingerprint the user read and approved (greffon_lire's or greffon_projet's Greffon empreinte): a plugin whose files changed since is refused.

greffon.description: The plugin as now installed, read from its new folder (source utilisateur), without its files.

remplace.description: The version of the user's plugin it replaced; null when none was installed.

erreurs.message: Model not found: <numero>
erreurs.quand: Without chemin, numero names no model of the project.

erreurs.message: Model <name> doesn't have its plugin.
erreurs.quand: That model isn't a plugin's (no copy of a plugin in its definition).

erreurs.message: The plugin has errors: it can't be installed.
erreurs.quand: Its manifest or its code has errors (Greffon's erreurs); greffon_lire's raison says this refusal and the four that follow beforehand.

erreurs.message: Your organisation's policy (DisableCustomCode) only allows the plugins it provides.
erreurs.quand: The DisableCustomCode policy is on.

erreurs.message: Plugins are installed from the desktop application.
erreurs.quand: The engine has no user's plugins folder (NUEE_GREFFONS empty: started by hand).

erreurs.message: Your organisation already provides this plugin (version <version>): its own is used.
erreurs.quand: The organisation's folder has a valid plugin of that id.

erreurs.message: It needs Nuée <version> or newer (this one: <version>).
erreurs.quand: Its manifest's nuee is above this Nuée's version.

erreurs.message: The plugin changed since you read it: read it again before installing it.
erreurs.quand: empreinte is missing or isn't the fingerprint of the plugin as read now.

erreurs.message: The installed version of <id> can't be replaced (a file in use?).
erreurs.quand: The folder of the version installed couldn't be moved aside; nothing changed.

erreurs.message: The plugin <id> can't be written into <folder>.
erreurs.quand: The new folder couldn't take the name <id>; the version installed is put back.

erreurs.message: cannot open the connection
erreurs.quand: A file can't be written into the user's plugins folder (R's own message, untranslated).

greffon_installer.effet_detail: Writes files outside any project: the plugin's plugin.json and the R files its manifest lists go into a hidden folder of the user's plugins folder (created when missing), renamed <id> once whole; the folder of that name before it is moved aside, then deleted (put back when the rename fails). No project changes; the plugin is in the lists of greffons and etat from then on. It isn't approved by this: until its fingerprint is approved (code_approuve, which the application sends first), its permis is false.

greffon_retirer.but: Removes one of the user's plugins, as File › Plugins… › Remove does.

id.description: The plugin's id (Greffon's id), a plugin of the user's plugins folder; the organisation's aren't removed.

erreurs.message: No plugin <id> among yours (your organisation's aren't removed here).
erreurs.quand: No folder of the user's plugins folder holds a plugin of that id, valid or not (also without id).

erreurs.message: The folder <folder> can't be deleted (a file in use?).
erreurs.quand: The plugin's folder is still there after its deletion; some of its files may be gone.

greffon_retirer.effet_detail: Deletes the plugin's folder from the user's plugins folder, outside any project: it leaves greffons, etat and New model. No project changes: its approval stays, and the models that carry it are still fitted with their own copy.

greffon_projet.but: Gives the plugins a project's models carry, with their code, their models, whether they may run here and the installed version of the same id, for Show in the bar above the project.

greffons.description: One per plugin its PLUGIN models carry, one per fingerprint (a copy with errors too, etat invalide; a definition without its copy is left out), each source projet with its fichiers and three fields more: modeles, its models in the project, [{nom, numero (null without)}] (always an array); interdit, whether the DisableCustomCode policy keeps it from running here (it isn't the organisation's); installe, the usable installed plugin of the same id (the organisation's when it gives one), {version, empreinte, source, ordre (1 when the project's version is newer, -1 older, 0 the same), meme (the same files)}, null when there is none. Always an array.

greffon_mettre_a_jour.but: Moves a project's models made with a plugin to its installed version, each redefined with its inputs and options, to be fitted again (Use version <version>, in the bar above the project).

id.description: The plugin's id; its usable installed version is the one taken (the organisation's when it gives one).

numeros.description: Only the models of these numbers (ResumeModele's numero); without it, every model of the project made with that plugin.
The numbers of the definitions changed, to fit again (ajuster with numero); always an array, empty when none changed.

refus.description: The definitions the installed version doesn't take, each {nom, erreur}: its name, and why in the request's language (ajuster's refusals of a plugin's definition: a variable an input no longer accepts, a new input without a variable…); always an array.

erreurs.message: The plugin <id> isn't installed.
erreurs.quand: No usable plugin of that id is installed (Greffon's etat ok; also without id).

greffon_mettre_a_jour.effet_detail: When at least one definition changed: one undo step, labelled update to the plugin <id> <version>, and the project counts as modified. Each changed definition carries the installed version's copy (its fingerprint, version and files), and keeps the inputs and options that version still has (the others dropped, its new options at their defaults); the definitions already at that version, those numeros leaves out and those refused stay as they were. No model is fitted again: the session's fitted models stay as they were, until each definition is fitted with ajuster and its numero.

predire.but: Predicts the project's observations, or one of its prediction sets, with a fitted model.

modele.description: The fitted model's id. It predicts on the project as it saw it: each qualitative variable's categories in their order at its fit (those added since after them), with the definition of that fit, so that categories put in another order since don't change its predictions.

jeu.description: A prediction set of a .usp project, by its rank in Projet's predictions, from 1; without it, every observation of the project.

observations.description: A table, one row per observation predicted. PCA and PLS: t1…tA, T2, DModX, DModX_pondere, "<y> prédit" (PLS), classe_predite (PLS-DA); a regression: "<y> prédit" on the modelled scale, "<y> observé" when known, categorie_inconnue (a category the model hasn't seen, left without a prediction) when there is one; another analysis: its own (a k-means: "groupe prédit", "distance au centre"); then hors_domaine (outside the model's domain: DModX above DCrit or T2 above T2Crit(95%), a regression's term outside its range), uid, nom, dans_modele (an observation of the model).

erreurs.message: Unknown prediction set: <jeu> (the project has <n>).
erreurs.quand: jeu isn't the rank of one of the project's prediction sets.

erreurs.message: predict() didn't predict these observations: <R's message>
erreurs.quand: An R-code or plugin model whose fit's predict() fails on these observations, or doesn't give one prediction per observation (predict() didn't give one prediction per observation.).

predire.effet_detail: The predictions are kept in the session, the last ones of each model, for exporter_prediction.

predire_fichier.but: Predicts the rows of a table file with a fitted model, the file's columns matched to the model's variables by name.

modele.description: The fitted model's id. It reads the file on the project as it saw it: the categories in their order at its fit, with the definition of that fit.

chemin.description: The file on the engine's computer, in a format File › Open reads (CSV, Excel…); from a browser, the path /api/deposer gives. Its columns are found by the variables' names, case and surrounding spaces aside, a qualitative variable's values by its categories' names; a model's quantitative variable is read as numbers. A hierarchical model's missing scores of base models ($M1.t1…) are predicted by the latest model of that name fitted in the session, refused as the model itself would be when its variables or categories changed since its fit.

observations.description: A table, one row per row of the file: the columns of predire's, without uid, nom the rows' names as the file gives them, dans_modele false.

absentes.description: The model's X variables the file hasn't, left missing (one name may come as a single string).

note.description: What to know of the reading: values read as missing in the model's X columns, a regression's effort missing from the file (predictions for an effort of 1) (always an array).

erreurs.message: This file holds no table (data frame or matrix)
erreurs.quand: An R file (.rds, .RData) holds no table.

erreurs.message: cannot open the connection
erreurs.quand: The file exists but can't be read (R's own message).

erreurs.message: predict() didn't predict these observations: <R's message>
erreurs.quand: An R-code or plugin model whose fit's predict() fails on these observations, or doesn't give one prediction per observation (predict() didn't give one prediction per observation.).

predire_fichier.effet_detail: The predictions are kept in the session, the last ones of each model, for exporter_prediction.

hca.but: Clusters a PCA or PLS model's observations by Ward's method on their scores, and cuts the tree into groups.

modele.description: The fitted model's id: a PCA, PLS or OPLS (not a regression or another analysis).

composantes.description: How many components' scores (t1, t2…) make the Euclidean distances between observations, from 1 to the model's A; the model's A by default.

groupes.description: The number of clusters to cut the tree into; brought back to the number of observations in the tree when larger.

composantes.description: The number of components whose scores were used.

merge.description: hclust's merge matrix, one [a, b] row per fusion: a negative number -j is the observation at position j of uid, a positive one the cluster made at that earlier row.

hauteurs.description: Each fusion's Ward height, the increase of the within-group sum of squares of the scores (hclust's ward.D2 height squared over 2); they add up to the scores' total sum of squares.

ordre.description: The order of the leaves for drawing the tree, as positions in uid.

noms.description: The observations' names, in the order of uid.

uid.description: The numbers of the model's observations that have all the scores used (the others are left out), in the model's order.

groupes.description: Each observation's cluster, 1 the largest, in the order of uid.

k.description: The number of clusters: groupes, at most the number of observations in the tree.

erreurs.message: The dendrogram is made on 1 to <A> components (the model's): <composantes>.
erreurs.quand: composantes is below 1 or above the model's number of components.

erreurs.message: elements of 'k' must be between 1 and <n>
erreurs.quand: groupes is below 1 (R's own message from cutree, untranslated).

permutations.but: Tests a PLS model by refitting it with its Y permuted among its observations, and gives each refit's R² and Q² with their regression lines on the correlation to the original Y.

modele.description: The fitted model's id: a PLS, PLS-DA, OPLS or OPLS-DA.

y.description: Which Y is permuted and measured, by its position among the model's Y (1 the first, their number at most); for a PLS-DA, every class is permuted together and y chooses the class indicator whose R² and Q² are measured.

n.description: The number of permutations; a value outside 1 to 999 is brought back within it. Each refit redoes the whole model (scaling and cross-validation included) with the same number of components; the permutations come from a fixed seed, the same at each call.

y.description: The name of the Y measured.

points.description: A table (columns), the model itself first then one row per permutation: correlation (the absolute correlation between the original and the permuted Y, 1 for the model), R2 and Q2 (that Y's cumulative R² and Q²), origine (true for the model itself).

ordonnee_R2.description: The intercept of the regression line of R2 on the correlation: with ordonnee_Q2, a measure of overfitting (a valid model usually has R2 below 0.3 to 0.4 and Q2 below 0.05 there).

ordonnee_Q2.description: The intercept of the regression line of Q2 on the correlation.

erreurs.message: The permutation test only applies to PLS models
erreurs.quand: The model is a PCA.

erreurs.message: The model has no Y number <y>: it has <n>.
erreurs.quand: y isn't one of 1 to the model's number of Y (for a PLS-DA, of classes).

contributions.but: Gives each X term's contribution to how far an observation, or the mean of several, lies from a PCA or PLS model (DModX) or from the model's centre (a score, T²).

modele.description: The fitted model's id: a PCA, PLS or OPLS.

observations.description: The observations' numbers; several give the contributions to their mean, and those that aren't in the model are left out.

valeurs.DModX: Each term's scaled residual, as in the distance to the model
valeurs.score: The distance to the mean observation in scaled units, times the absolute weight of the component composante (w* in a PLS, p in a PCA)
valeurs.T2: The same with the weights of all the components together, for an observation outside the ellipse

composante.description: With type score: the component, from 1 to the model's A.

ponderee.description: With type DModX: each residual multiplied by its variable's modelling power, as the weighted DModX.

terme.description: The model's X terms, in its order.

contribution.description: Each term's contribution, in the order of terme.

erreurs.message: None of the chosen observations is in the model
erreurs.quand: No observation given is one of the model's.

erreurs.message: "<type>" isn't a choice of contributions: DModX, score, T2.
erreurs.quand: type is none of its values.

erreurs.message: Component <composante>: the model has <A>.
erreurs.quand: With type score, composante is below 1 or beyond the model's number of components.

appartenance.but: Gives each observation's distance to every model of a group of class models, the classes whose model accepts it, and the share of each known class that each model accepts.

modele.description: The id of one fitted model of the group (made by modeles_classe); the group's other models are those of the session, the latest of each name, or fitted for this request when there are none.

observations.description: A table (columns), one row per observation of the project, those no model saw included: uid, nom, classe (its known class, null without one), one column "DModX <class>" per class (its distance to that class's model), classes (the classes whose model accepts it, DModX at most the model's DCrit at 5 %, comma-separated; "" for none).

classes.description: The classes of the group, one per model.

dcrit.description: Each model's critical distance DCrit at 5 %, in the order of classes (the names R gives it are lost in JSON).

table.description: One row per known class, then "?" for the observations without one: {classe, n (its observations), parts (the share of them each model accepts, in the order of classes; always an array)}.

erreurs.message: This model isn't part of a group of class models
erreurs.quand: The model wasn't made by modeles_classe.

appartenance.effet_detail: A model of the group that isn't fitted in the session is fitted for the request, and not kept.

spectres.but: Gives a model's spectra, its quantitative X variables for its observations, as read and after its spectral preprocessing.

modele.description: The fitted model's id: a PCA, PLS or OPLS.

valeurs.bruts: The spectra as read only (each value transformed as the model transforms it)
valeurs.pretraites: The preprocessed spectra only (SNV, MSC, derivatives…; the same as read without preprocessing)

quoi.description: Which spectra to send; both without it (any other value gives neither).

noms.description: The quantitative X terms, in the model's order (always an array).

uid.description: The model's observations, in its order: the rows of bruts and pretraites.

bruts.description: One row per observation, one value per term, rounded to 6 significant digits; null unless asked.

pretraites.description: The same after the model's spectral preprocessing; null unless asked.

biplot.but: Gives a PCA or PLS model's scores and loadings scaled to correlations, for a biplot within the unit circle.

modele.description: The fitted model's id: a PCA, PLS or OPLS.

t.description: One array per component: each observation's score divided by the norm of that component's scores (null for an observation without scores).

p.description: One array per component: each X term's correlation with the scores, on the observations where it has a value (null under 3 of them, or without variation).

c.description: The same for each Y of a PLS; null for a PCA.

noms_x.description: The X terms, in the order of p's arrays (always an array).

noms_y.description: The Y terms, in the order of c's arrays (always an array, empty for a PCA).

ipls.but: Fits interval PLS models on consecutive ranges of a model's spectrum and gives each range's RMSEcv for 1 to A components (iPLS, Nørgaard et al. 2000).

modele.description: The fitted model's id: a PLS, PLS-DA or OPLS whose quantitative X make a spectrum (an OPLS is fitted as a PLS).

n.description: The number of intervals of about the same width, at most the number of spectrum variables (brought back within that range).

A.description: Up to how many components each interval's PLS is fitted with; the model's A by default.

intervalles.description: One per interval, in the spectrum's order: {termes, variables (its terms and their variables' numbers), rmsecv (for 1, 2… A components, null where even one component doesn't fit), A (the number that gives the smallest RMSEcv, null if none)}; the arrays always arrays.

complet.description: The same for the whole spectrum, {rmsecv, A}: it gives the model back.

A.description: The largest number of components tried.

spectre.description: The spectrum's terms, in order (always an array).

moyen.description: The mean preprocessed spectrum, one value per term of spectre (always an array).

autres.description: The model's other X terms (qualitative ones, cross terms), in every interval's model (always an array).

erreurs.message: iPLS needs a model with Y (PLS, PLS-DA, OPLS).
erreurs.quand: The model is a PCA.

erreurs.message: iPLS needs quantitative X variables (a spectrum).
erreurs.quand: The model has fewer than 2 quantitative X terms.

effets.but: Gives the effect of each quantitative term of a regression along its variable's values, on the link's scale with its 95 % band, one per category for a term crossed with categories, or with echelle reponse the response's predicted values.

valeurs.lien: The effects on the link's scale, centred (any other value too)
valeurs.reponse: The predicted values of the response, on its scale (Plots › Effects › Predicted values)

echelle.description: The scale of the result; reponse gives the predicted values, with fields of their own (echelle, commun, and each term's fixes).
With echelle reponse: "reponse"; absent on the link's scale.

lien.description: The model's link: identity, log, logit…

effets.description: One per quantitative term, main effects first, then the terms that only enter through a cross term with categories. A term alone: {terme, courbe (a smooth curve, else a straight line), x (80 values over the variable's range, in its units, transformed if it is), effet (centred on the variable's mean, the other terms fixed), bas, haut (the 95 % band), valeurs (the observed values)}. A term crossed with categories: {terme, courbe, par (their variables, "a × b"), valeurs, niveaux: one {niveau, x, effet, bas, haut, valeurs, and for a straight line pente, pente_bas, pente_haut per unit of the variable} per category observed}. A curve per category: {terme, courbe: true, par_categorie: true, par, valeurs, niveaux: one {niveau, x, effet, bas, haut, valeurs} per category}. With echelle reponse, the same terms, order and shapes, without slopes: effet, bas and haut are the response's predicted values and their band (the inverse link of the linear predictor and of its ± 1.96 standard errors; the response as modelled for an identity link; a zero-inflated Poisson's expected count), not centred; the model's other quantitative variables at their mean on its observations (before their transformation), its qualitative ones at their reference category, but those crossed with the term, each category of which has its line, x over the term's values in that category; each term adds fixes, what stays fixed for it ({quantitatives: a table nom, valeur; qualitatives: a table nom, categorie}), and each line grille, its grid (for the export to R).

commun.description: With echelle reponse: what stays fixed for every term, {aleatoires (the random effects' levels, at 0: the population; always an array), decalage (the effort variable's name, at 1: densities; null without one), spatial ({nom, x, y}: the spatial smooth at the coordinates' mean point; null without one)}.

erreurs.message: The values of "<term>" have changed since this model was fitted: fit it again.
erreurs.quand: With echelle reponse, a quantitative variable's values in the project no longer give the model's columns.

effets.effet_detail: Computed once for each scale and kept with the fitted model: later calls give the kept result.

seuils.but: Gives a GAM curve's effect and slope with simultaneous 95 % bands, and the ranges where the slope is clearly positive or negative, as thresholds (Simpson 2018).

modele.description: The fitted regression's id: a GAM, or a model with a curve fitted by mgcv.

terme.description: The curve's term, by its name as in the model's coefficients and curves.

categorie.description: For a curve per category (s(x, by = f)) or a curve crossed with categories: the category whose curve to read; the first without it.
Only for a curve with categories: the category read.

par.description: Only for a curve with categories: its qualitative variable or variables ("a × b").

edf.description: The curve's effective degrees of freedom.

p.description: The p of the curve's test (mgcv).

lineaire.description: edf below 1.5: the curve is almost a straight line.

amplitude.description: The range of the effect over the grid.

x.description: 200 values from the 2nd to the 98th percentile of the variable (in that category), in the variable's units.

effet.description: The curve at x, on the link's scale, centred on its mean.

bas.description: The lower edge of its simultaneous 95 % band (2000 draws of the coefficients, a fixed seed).

haut.description: The upper edge of that band.

x_pente.description: The 199 midpoints between consecutive values of x.

pente.description: The curve's slope at x_pente, per unit of the variable.

pente_bas.description: The lower edge of the slope's simultaneous 95 % band.

sens.description: At each midpoint: "hausse" (the band of the slope is above 0), "baisse" (below 0) or "ns".

plages_pente.description: A table (columns) of the ranges where the slope is clearly positive or negative: sens ("hausse" or "baisse"), de, a (from, to).

plages_effet.description: A table (columns) of the ranges where the effect is clearly above or below its mean: sens ("au_dessus" or "au_dessous"), de, a.

critique_effet.description: The critical multiplier of the effect's simultaneous band.

tirages.description: The number of draws of the coefficients, 2000.

valeurs.description: The variable's observed values (in that category), in its units: a rug.

erreurs.message: Thresholds are read on a curve of an additive model.
erreurs.quand: The regression wasn't fitted by mgcv: an LM, or an LMM fitted by nlme.

erreurs.message: "<term>" is not a curve of this model.
erreurs.quand: terme names no curve of the model.

erreurs.message: "<category>" is not a category of the curve of "<term>".
erreurs.quand: categorie names no category of that curve, or the curve has none.

seuils.effet_detail: Computed once per term and category and kept with the fitted model: later calls give the kept result.

apports.but: Gives what each group of terms brings to a regression, from the model refitted by maximum likelihood without it: the change of AIC and the likelihood-ratio test.

apports.description: A table (columns), one row per group of terms (its block in New model, else its variable): groupe, termes (how many terms leave with it), delta_aic (the AIC without it minus the full model's, both ML: above 0 the group improves the model, above 2 clearly), khi2, ddl, p (the likelihood-ratio test; null when the refit fails), avec (the groups that leave with it, the cross terms that need it, comma-separated). An empty object {} for a model without terms.

apports.effet_detail: Computed once and kept with the fitted model: later calls give the kept result.

selection_aic.but: Selects a regression's fixed effects by AICc over every allowed combination of its groups of terms, or by backward elimination beyond 256 combinations, each candidate refitted by maximum likelihood.

modele.description: The fitted regression's id. Its random effects, autocorrelation, distribution, offset and curves' settings stay those of the model; a cross term enters only with its main effects; the groups that carry a random slope stay in every candidate.

K.description: The number of groups chosen among. With 0, the result has only K, N and gardes.

N.description: The model's number of observations, those of every candidate.

gardes.description: The groups kept in every candidate: those carrying a random slope and those they need (always an array).

methode.description: "toutes" (every combination, 2^K at most limite) or "descendante" (backward elimination: at each step, the removal that lowers AICc the most).

limite.description: The most combinations fitted all together, 256.

groupes.description: The groups chosen among, by name (always an array).

termes.description: Each group's terms, in the order of groupes.

requis.description: The groups each group needs (a cross term, its main effects), in the order of groupes.

modeles.description: A table (columns) of the candidates, by increasing AICc (failed fits last): modele (its groups, "a + b", "1" for the null model), n_groupes, k (parameters), logLik, AICc, delta (ΔAICc), poids (Akaike weight), poids_cumule, etape (the step of the backward elimination, null for every combination).

contient.description: For each group, in the order of groupes: 1 or 0 for each row of modeles, whether it contains that group.

importance.description: A table (columns): groupe, importance (the sum of the weights of the candidates that contain it).

meilleur.description: The row of modeles of the best candidate, the lowest AICc: 1.

parcimonieux.description: The row of the most parsimonious candidate: the fewest parameters among those with ΔAICc at most 2.

chemin.description: The backward elimination's steps, a table (columns) etape, retire (the group removed), AICc; null for every combination.

echecs.description: The number of candidates whose fit failed.

erreurs.message: No model has an AICc: too few observations for their parameters.
erreurs.quand: Every candidate's fit failed or has no AICc.

selection_aic.effet_detail: Computed once and kept with the fitted model: methodes then describes the selection and script_r redoes it.

autocorrelation_residus.but: Gives the autocorrelation of a regression's residuals along time within groups, pooled as nlme's ACF, to see whether a CAR1 autocorrelation is needed or is enough.

modele.description: The fitted regression's id. A model with CAR1 uses its own time and groups, and the next two parameters are ignored.

temps.description: The time, an identifier ({by: "id", id}) or a variable ({by: "variable", variable}), numbers or dates; required without CAR1. Several: the first.

groupe.description: The groups within which the residuals follow each other, nested from the widest to the finest; {by: "effets"} stands for the model's random effects. Without it, all the observations make one series.

valeurs.deviance: Each observation's signed part of the deviance

type.description: The residuals of a model fitted by mgcv alone (a GLM, a GAM); the others' are Pearson's.

phi.description: Its CAR1 φ, null without CAR1.

groupe.description: The groups' names, "site / sector"; null for one series.

laissees.description: The model's observations left out, without a time or a group.

decalage.description: The lags, 0 to min(10, the longest series minus 1): successive observations of a series, not units of time.

paires.description: The pairs of observations at each lag.

bande.description: ±1.96/√pairs at each lag: the band of nlme's plot.

series.description: {residus, acf (one value per lag)}: the residuals (residus "pearson" or "deviance"), and with CAR1 a second series of its normalized residuals ("normalises"), which show no autocorrelation left when CAR1 accounts for it.

erreurs.message: Choose the time (a year, a date...): an ID or a variable.
erreurs.quand: temps is missing and the model has no CAR1.

erreurs.message: This project has no ID "<id>".
erreurs.quand: A grouping by id names no identifier of the observations.

erreurs.message: Unknown grouping "<by>"
erreurs.quand: A grouping's by is none of id and variable (or effets for groupe).

erreurs.message: The time (<name>) must be numbers (the year) or dates (2019-05-14, 14/05/2019): <why>
erreurs.quand: The time is made of dates and one of its values isn't a date (variables.R: refus_temps).

erreurs.message: This model has no random effect.
erreurs.quand: groupe has {by: "effets"} and the model has no random effect.

erreurs.message: No observation of the model has both a time and a group.
erreurs.quand: Every observation lacks its time or its group.

erreurs.message: Several observations have the same time in the same group: choose finer groups (the sector within its site...).
erreurs.quand: Two observations of a group share a time.

erreurs.message: Each group has a single observation: no autocorrelation to compute.
erreurs.quand: No series has two observations.

erreurs.message: "<type>" isn't a choice of residuals: pearson, deviance.
erreurs.quand: type is none of its values for a model fitted by mgcv alone.

rapports_vraisemblance.but: Gives the likelihood-ratio tests between the nested pairs among some regressions that differ only by their fixed effects, as anova(m1, m2) on their maximum-likelihood fits.

modeles.description: The fitted models' ids, each a model of the session; those that aren't regressions are left out without an error. Two are compared when they have the same response, observations, distribution, effort, random effects (slopes included) and autocorrelation, and one's fixed terms lie within the other's.

paires.description: A table (columns), one row per nested pair: grand, petit (the bigger and the smaller model's ids), ddl, khi2 (2 × the difference of their ML log-likelihoods, 0 at least), p, approche (true when one has curves or mgcv random effects: edf, an approximate test). An empty object {} without any pair.

total.description: The number of nested pairs found.

max.description: At most that many pairs are given, 2000.

coefficients_modeles.but: Puts several regressions' coefficients side by side with their fit statistics, as the cells of a table for an article.

modeles.description: The fitted regressions' ids, in the order of the columns.

erreur.description: What follows each estimate; any other value is ic.

modeles.description: The columns' names: the models' names, made unique with a number (always an array).

entete.description: The header of the terms' column ("Estimate [95% CI]", "Estimate (SE)").

termes.description: The rows: the first model's terms, then the next ones' that it hasn't (always an array).

cellules.description: One row per term, one cell per model: the estimate with its interval or standard error, as text with the decimal mark of the request's language; "" when the model hasn't the term.

p.description: Each cell's p, null where the model hasn't the term.

statistiques.description: The fit rows that some model has: n, AIC, AICc, R², marginal and conditional R², deviance explained, the distribution's parameters, σ of each random effect and of the residual, ρ of random slopes, φ (CAR1), each curve's edf (always an array).

valeurs.description: One row per fit statistic, one cell per model, as text.

note_lien.description: What the estimates mean for a model with a log or logit link; null when every link is the identity.

copie.description: The same table for the clipboard: {entetes (always an array), lignes (rows of text: the terms with their cells, the p's stars added, then the fit rows), notes (the stars' legend and the link's note, always an array)}.

erreurs.message: Tick at least one regression.
erreurs.quand: modeles is empty.

erreurs.message: Only regressions (LM, LMM, GLM, GAM) go side by side.
erreurs.quand: A model isn't a regression.

puissance_tendance.but: Computes the power of monitoring designs to detect a trend with a linear regression or a linear mixed model's variances, and on request checks one design by simulation.

modele.description: The fitted regression's id: an LM, or an LMM fitted by nlme (with or without CAR1), with random intercepts only and a quantitative untransformed X for the time. Without any of the parameters below (one this request doesn't take doesn't count), the result of the last computation for this model (its sentence in the request's language), else the defaults.

terme.description: The time: the name of a quantitative, untransformed X term of the model. By default the first whose name looks like a time (year, date, time, season, année…), else the CAR1 time's variable, else the first such term.

valeurs.pente: A slope in the response's units per unit of time
valeurs.pourcent: A change in % per year, for a response in log10 or ln

unite.description: The trend's unit; pourcent by default for a response in log10 or ln, else pente (any other value: the default).

tendance.description: The trend to detect, not 0; by default -3 (% per year), or in pente minus 3 % of the mean response's absolute value, rounded to 2 significant digits.

alpha.description: The level of the two-sided test.

annees.description: The first and last numbers of years of the curves, whole numbers from 3 to 100; by default 5 to the data's span or 30, whichever is larger, 100 at most (another number of values than two: the default).

unites.description: The numbers of units (the first random effect's, or observations per year for an LM) of the curves, whole numbers from 2 (1 for an LM) to 10000; the data's own number is always added, 10 numbers at most. By default the data's number times 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 2.

simulation.description: The simulation's design, {annees (3 to 100, by default the data's span), unites (by default the data's), n (data sets, 10 to 2000, by default 200)}; its expected duration is in estimation.

simuler.description: true to run the simulation now, unless one with the same settings is kept; refused beyond 20000 observations per data set or about 15 minutes.

reglages.description: The settings used: {terme, unite, tendance, alpha, annees ([first, last], always an array), unites (always an array), simulation {annees, unites, n}}.

termes.description: The X terms that can be the time (always an array).

pourcent_possible.description: Whether the response is in log10 or ln, so a trend in % can be given.

approchee.description: A trend in % on log(a·y + c) with c not 0: an approximation.

transformation.description: The response's transformation, as text ("" without one).

forme.description: That transformation as the definition keeps it; null without one.

pente.description: The slope to detect on the response's scale, per unit of time.

pente_modele.description: The model's own slope of the time, in its units, for comparison.

y_modele.description: The response as written with its transformation.

niveaux.description: The random effects' levels, from the widest (always an array, empty for an LM).

dans.description: The finer group within which CAR1 runs, if any.

temps_car1.description: The CAR1 time's name, if any.

croises.description: The model's cross terms with the time, left out of the designs (always an array).

plan.description: The data's design: {annees (years spanned), N, unites, emboites and moyennes (nested units per level, rounded and mean; always arrays), dans, moyenne_dans (CAR1 groups in the finest unit), repetitions, moyenne_repetitions (observations per series and year), series_par_unite}.

variances.description: The model's REML variances: {sigma2 (residual), niveaux (each random effect's; always an array), phi (CAR1's φ, null without CAR1)}.

tableau.description: A table (columns), one row per design: annees, unites, observations, erreur_type (of the GLS slope), puissance.

seuil.description: 0.8, the power that annees_80 looks for.

annees_80.description: A table (columns): unites, annees (the fewest years for 80 % power, null when the curves don't reach it).

estimation.description: The simulation's cost: {plan ([years, units, series per unit, repetitions]), par_ajustement (seconds per fit, null for a design too big), duree (seconds expected for n data sets), observations (per data set)}.

simulation.description: The simulation once run with these settings, else null: {annees, unites, n, graine, alpha, observations, puissance (the share of p at most alpha), erreur_mc (its Monte Carlo error), echecs, duree (seconds), p (each data set's p), cle (the settings it was run with), analytique (the formula's power at that design)}.

phrase.description: The sentence for a report, at the data's number of units, in the request's language (X-Langue).

erreurs.message: Trend power is computed for a linear regression or a linear mixed model (nlme), with a normal response: not for a generalized or additive model (GLM, GAM), whose distribution and mgcv fit aren't covered.
erreurs.quand: The model is a GLM or a GAM, or was fitted by mgcv.

erreurs.message: This model has random slopes: trend power covers random intercepts only.
erreurs.quand: A random effect has random slopes.

erreurs.message: This model has no time among its quantitative X (untransformed): the trend is the slope of an X, the year. Add it as an X variable.
erreurs.quand: No quantitative X term is left untransformed.

erreurs.message: "<term>" isn't a quantitative X (untransformed) of this model: choose the time among <terms>.
erreurs.quand: terme names no such term.

erreurs.quand: tendance is 0, or not a finite number.

erreurs.message: α is between 0.001 and 0.2.
erreurs.quand: alpha is outside that range.

erreurs.quand: unite is pourcent and the response isn't in log10 or ln.

erreurs.message: A decline of 100% or more has no logarithm.
erreurs.quand: unite is pourcent and tendance is -100 or less.

moyennes.but: Gives a regression's adjusted means of the categories of a qualitative X, or a quantitative X's slope in each category, and the pairs of categories compared, as the emmeans package computes them.

modele.description: The fitted regression's id. Without any of the parameters below (one this request doesn't take doesn't count), the settings of its last computation in the session, else the defaults.

facteur.description: The qualitative X variable whose categories' means are computed, by its number; the model's first qualitative variable by default.

dans.description: A qualitative variable crossed with facteur in a term of the model, by its number: facteur's categories are compared within each of its categories (simple effects).

pente.description: A quantitative variable crossed with facteur in a term, by its number: its slope in each category instead of the means (as emtrends).

valeurs.holm: Holm's p values and Bonferroni intervals

ajustement.description: How the pairs' p values and intervals are adjusted, within each category of dans.

valeurs.reponse: On the response's scale: means, and ratios (odds ratios for a logit link) for the pairs

echelle.description: The scale of a model with a log or logit link (slopes stay on the link's scale).

reglages.description: The settings used: {facteur (the variable's number as text), dans, pente, ajustement, echelle}.

forme_y.description: The response as written with its transformation, null without one.

log_y.description: Whether the response is in log10 or ln.

echelle.description: The scale of the estimates: "reponse", "identite" (an identity link) or "lien".

facteur.description: {uid, nom, niveaux (its observed categories, always an array)}.

dans.description: The same for dans, null without it.

pente.description: With pente: {uid, nom, terme, delta (the step of the forward difference), forme}; null without it.

grille.description: The reference grid: {lignes, covariables (a table: terme, nom, moyenne, valeur, transformee, courbe; each quantitative variable at its mean), moyennees (the qualitative variables averaged over, always an array), decalage, spatial ({nom, x, y}: a spatial smooth at the mean point)}.

croisee.description: The variables crossed with facteur that dans or pente can name (always an array).

ddl.description: {methode ("residuels", "confinement" for nlme, or "asymptotique": z), groupe, groupes (nlme's first random effect and its number of groups)}.

moyennes.description: A table (columns), one row per estimable category (or pair of categories with dans): niveau, groupe (dans's category, null without dans), estimation, erreur_type, ddl, bas, haut (95 %), lien, erreur_type_lien (on the link's scale).

paires.description: A table (columns), one row per estimable pair within each category of dans: groupe, niveau_1, niveau_2, difference, erreur_type_lien, ddl, t, p_brute, p (adjusted), famille (the family size of the adjustment), bas_lien, haut_lien, estimation, erreur_type, bas, haut (on the result's scale).

non_estimables.description: {moyennes, paires}: the categories and pairs left out because no observation has them (always arrays).

options.description: The choices for each qualitative variable of the model: {uid, nom, niveaux, dans: [{uid, nom}], pentes: [{uid, nom}]}.

phrases.description: A sentence for a report per pair, in the order of paires, in the request's language (X-Langue; always an array).

erreurs.quand: The model has no qualitative X.
